creators.name: Harun Farocki
creators.bio: German filmmaker, writer and installation artist who made over 90 films and installations on images, labour and war.
creators.why: He coined the term 'operational images': pictures made by machines for machines, a founding idea for machine-vision art.
creators.bio_zh: 德国电影人、作家与装置艺术家，创作了 90 多部关于图像、劳动与战争的影片和装置。
creators.why_zh: 他提出“操作图像”（由机器生成、供机器读取的图像）这一概念，是机器视觉艺术的奠基思想。

creators.name: Trevor Paglen
creators.bio: American artist and geographer whose photographs, installations and performances investigate surveillance, secrecy and computer vision.
creators.why: His works on training sets, facial recognition and 'invisible images' made the machine's way of seeing a central subject of contemporary art.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、地理学家
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家与地理学家，以摄影、装置和表演研究监控、国家机密与计算机视觉。
creators.why_zh: 他关于训练数据集、人脸识别和“不可见图像”的作品，让机器的观看方式成为当代艺术的核心议题。
creators.based_zh: 柏林，德国 / 纽约，美国

creators.name: Kate Crawford
creators.role: Researcher and author; Research Professor, USC Annenberg
creators.bio: Australian scholar of the social and political implications of AI, co-founder of the AI Now Institute and author of Atlas of AI (2021).
creators.why: With Trevor Paglen and Vladan Joler she turned the critique of datasets and AI infrastructure into widely seen exhibitions and maps.
creators.role_zh: 研究者、作家；南加州大学安嫩伯格学院研究教授
creators.bio_zh: 澳大利亚学者，研究 AI 的社会与政治影响，AI Now 研究所联合创始人，著有《Atlas of AI》（2021）。
creators.why_zh: 她与 Trevor Paglen、Vladan Joler 合作，把对数据集与 AI 基础设施的批判变成了广为人知的展览与图谱。

creators.name: Memo Akten
creators.role: Artist and researcher; Assistant Professor, UC San Diego
creators.bio: Turkish-born artist working with computation, machine learning and perception; PhD from Goldsmiths on AI and creativity.
creators.why: His Learning to See series makes neural-network perception a mirror for human bias in seeing.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、研究者；加州大学圣地亚哥分校助理教授
creators.bio_zh: 出生于土耳其的艺术家，以计算、机器学习与感知为创作材料，在伦敦大学金史密斯学院获 AI 与创造力方向博士。
creators.why_zh: 他的《Learning to See》系列把神经网络的感知变成一面镜子，映照人类观看中的偏见。

creators.name: Benjamin Grosser
creators.role: Artist; Professor, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
creators.bio: American artist who builds software and interactive works about the cultural, social and political effects of computing.
creators.why: His machine-vision works show what a computer 'looks at' and ask how that differs from human attention.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；伊利诺伊大学厄巴纳-香槟分校教授
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家，以软件和互动作品探讨计算对文化、社会与政治的影响。
creators.why_zh: 他的机器视觉作品展示计算机“在看什么”，追问它与人类注意力有何不同。

creators.name: David Rokeby
creators.bio: Canadian pioneer of interactive installation, known for Very Nervous System (1986–90) and works on machine perception and surveillance.
creators.why: Since 1990 his systems have staged machine seeing and naming as associative, fallible and political.
creators.role_zh: 装置艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 加拿大互动装置先驱，以《Very Nervous System》（1986–90）以及关于机器感知与监控的作品闻名。
creators.why_zh: 自 1990 年起，他的系统把机器的观看与命名呈现为联想式的、会出错的、带有政治性的过程。

creators.name: Myron Krueger
creators.bio: American computer artist (b. 1942) who built responsive environments from 1969 and coined the term 'artificial reality'.
creators.why: Videoplace was one of the first artworks in which a computer perceived the human body through a camera and answered it.
creators.role_zh: 计算机艺术家、研究者
creators.bio_zh: 美国计算机艺术家（生于 1942 年），1969 年起构建响应式环境，并提出“人工现实”一词。
creators.why_zh: 《Videoplace》是最早让计算机通过摄像头感知人体并作出回应的艺术作品之一。

creators.name: Jon Rafman
creators.bio: Canadian artist working with video, installation and found internet imagery.
creators.why: His Nine Eyes project was an early collection of the unintended images produced by an automated camera fleet.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、影像创作者
creators.bio_zh: 加拿大艺术家，以录像、装置和网络上的现成图像进行创作。
creators.why_zh: 他的《Nine Eyes》较早地收集了自动化相机车队无意间拍下的图像。

creators.name: Clement Valla
creators.role: Artist; teaches at Rhode Island School of Design
creators.bio: French-American artist whose works look at images and objects produced by automated systems and software.
creators.why: He shows that the strange images of automated systems are not errors but the system working exactly as designed.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；任教于罗德岛设计学院
creators.bio_zh: 法裔美国艺术家，研究由自动化系统和软件生成的图像与物件。
creators.why_zh: 他指出自动化系统产生的怪异图像并非错误，而正是系统按设计运行的结果。

creators.name: Esther Hovers
creators.bio: Dutch artist whose photographs and installations examine surveillance, power and normative behaviour in public space.
creators.why: False Positives visualises the behavioural 'anomalies' that intelligent surveillance cameras are trained to flag.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、摄影师
creators.bio_zh: 荷兰艺术家，以摄影和装置研究公共空间中的监控、权力与“正常行为”规范。
creators.why_zh: 《False Positives》把智能监控摄像头被训练去标记的“异常”行为变得可见。

creators.name: Nye Thompson
creators.bio: British artist who builds software systems that explore machine vision, surveillance networks and machine-made worldviews.
creators.why: Her AI entity The Seeker watched the world through insecure CCTV cameras and described what it saw.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 英国艺术家，构建软件系统来探讨机器视觉、监控网络与由机器生成的世界观。
creators.why_zh: 她创造的 AI 实体 The Seeker 通过不设防的监控摄像头观看世界，并描述它所看到的一切。

creators.name: Rosa Menkman
creators.bio: Dutch artist and theorist of glitch, compression and resolution, author of The Glitch Moment(um) (2011).
creators.why: Her research on colour test cards shows how the standards of image processing were calibrated on anonymous women's faces.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、理论家
creators.bio_zh: 荷兰艺术家与理论家，研究故障、压缩与分辨率，著有《The Glitch Moment(um)》（2011）。
creators.why_zh: 她对色彩测试卡的研究表明，图像处理的标准是以无名女性的面孔为基准校准的。

creators.name: Everest Pipkin
creators.bio: Everest Pipkin makes games, software, drawings and datasets-as-artworks, and writes on the ethics of corpora used for machine learning.
creators.bio_zh: Everest Pipkin 创作游戏、软件、绘画，并把数据集本身当作作品，长期书写机器学习语料的伦理问题。
creators.why: Pipkin's Lacework made an entire video training set watchable, turning the dataset into the subject.
creators.why_zh: Pipkin 的《Lacework》让一个完整的视频训练集可以被“观看”，把数据集本身变成了作品的主题。
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、游戏设计师、写作者

creators.name: Anna Ridler
creators.bio: Anna Ridler is a London-based artist who builds her own hand-made datasets and works with GANs to examine how collections of information are assembled.
creators.bio_zh: Anna Ridler 是常驻伦敦的艺术家，亲手制作自己的数据集，并用 GAN 探讨信息集合是如何被构建的。
creators.why: She treats the dataset as craft and labour, making visible the human work usually hidden inside machine learning.
creators.why_zh: 她把数据集视为手艺与劳动，让通常藏在机器学习背后的人工工作变得可见。
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、研究者

creators.name: Philipp Schmitt
creators.bio: Philipp Schmitt (b. 1993) is an artist and designer whose installations, artist books and websites engage with the philosophical, poetic and political sides of computation.
creators.bio_zh: Philipp Schmitt（1993 年生）是艺术家和设计师，以装置、艺术家书和网站探讨计算的哲学、诗意与政治面向。
creators.why: His works expose the training images, labels and photographers behind computer vision.
creators.why_zh: 他的作品揭示了计算机视觉背后的训练图像、标签以及拍下这些照片的人。
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、设计师

creators.name: Sebastian Schmieg
creators.bio: Sebastian Schmieg is a Berlin-based artist who works with found datasets, custom software, websites and lecture performances on the human labour inside algorithmic systems.
creators.bio_zh: Sebastian Schmieg 是常驻柏林的艺术家，用现成数据集、定制软件、网站和讲座表演，揭示算法系统中的人类劳动。
creators.why: He showed early how computer vision rests on crowd-workers' clicks and on arbitrary categories.
creators.why_zh: 他较早揭示了计算机视觉建立在众包工人的点击和武断的分类之上。
creators.role_zh: 艺术家

creators.name: Mushon Zer-Aviv
creators.bio: Mushon Zer-Aviv is a designer, educator and media activist who works on data, surveillance and algorithmic bias.
creators.bio_zh: Mushon Zer-Aviv 是设计师、教育者和媒体行动者，关注数据、监控与算法偏见。
creators.why: The Normalizing Machine turns visitors into the labellers of a face-based model of 'normal'.
creators.why_zh: 《The Normalizing Machine》让观众成为一个以人脸定义“正常”的模型的标注者。
creators.role_zh: 设计师、研究者、媒体行动者

creators.name: Forensic Architecture
creators.role: Research agency, Goldsmiths, University of London
creators.bio: Forensic Architecture, founded by Eyal Weizman in 2010, investigates state and corporate violence with spatial, architectural and computational methods and presents its findings in courts and museums.
creators.bio_zh: Forensic Architecture（法证建筑）由 Eyal Weizman 于 2010 年创立，用空间、建筑与计算方法调查国家和企业暴力，并在法庭与美术馆中呈现结果。
creators.why: It turns computer vision around: training classifiers on synthetic images to find evidence of human-rights abuses.
creators.why_zh: 它反转了计算机视觉的用途：用合成图像训练分类器，寻找侵犯人权的证据。
creators.role_zh: 研究机构，伦敦大学金史密斯学院

creators.name: Simone C. Niquille
creators.bio: Simone C. Niquille runs technoflesh Studio, making films and writing on computer vision, 3D capture and synthetic training datasets; they initiated the parametric truth Lab at Design Academy Eindhoven.
creators.bio_zh: Simone C. Niquille 主持 technoflesh Studio，以影片和写作研究计算机视觉、三维扫描与合成训练数据集，并在埃因霍温设计学院创办 parametric truth Lab。
creators.why: Their films show how domestic robots are taught to see homes through strange synthetic datasets.
creators.why_zh: 他们的影片展示了家用机器人如何通过古怪的合成数据集学习“看懂”家。
creators.role_zh: 设计师、研究者，technoflesh Studio

creators.name: Nouf Aljowaysir
creators.bio: Nouf Aljowaysir is a Saudi artist based in New York who works across photography and moving image, using dialogue with machines to examine migration, history and identity.
creators.bio_zh: Nouf Aljowaysir 是常驻纽约的沙特艺术家，以摄影和影像创作，借与机器的对话探讨迁徙、历史与身份。
creators.why: Her work shows how computer vision and generative AI misread and erase Arab identities.
creators.why_zh: 她的作品揭示了计算机视觉与生成式 AI 如何误读并抹除阿拉伯人的身份。
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、电影人

creators.name: Jake Elwes
creators.bio: Jake Elwes (b. 1993) is a London-based artist and researcher who has explored the aesthetics and ethics of machine learning since 2016, often with drag performers.
creators.bio_zh: Jake Elwes（1993 年生）是常驻伦敦的艺术家和研究者，自 2016 年起探索机器学习的美学与伦理，常与变装表演者合作。
creators.why: The Zizi Project queers facial datasets and shows what a network has and has not learned.
creators.why_zh: 《Zizi》项目以酷儿方式介入人脸数据集，显示神经网络学到了什么、没学到什么。
creators.role_zh: 艺术家

creators.name: Ursula Damm
creators.role: Artist; Professor of Media Environments, Bauhaus-Universität Weimar
creators.bio: Ursula Damm is a German media artist whose generative video installations use live camera input and neural networks to explore perception, urban space and nature.
creators.bio_zh: Ursula Damm 是德国媒体艺术家，她的生成影像装置以实时摄像输入和神经网络探讨感知、城市空间与自然。
creators.why: Membrane lets visitors steer how a neural network turns a street it watches into images of its own.
creators.why_zh: 《Membrane》让观众操控神经网络如何把它所观看的街道转化为它自己的图像。
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；包豪斯魏玛大学媒体环境教授

creators.name: Jia Deng
creators.role: Computer scientist; Associate Professor, Princeton University
creators.bio: Jia Deng is a computer-vision researcher who, as a PhD student with Fei-Fei Li, led the construction of the ImageNet dataset.
creators.bio_zh: 邓嘉是计算机视觉研究者，读博期间在李飞飞指导下主导构建了 ImageNet 数据集。
creators.why: ImageNet's categories and crowd-sourced labels became the worldview of modern computer vision, and a central object of critique for artists.
creators.why_zh: ImageNet 的类别体系和众包标签成为现代计算机视觉的世界观，也成为艺术家批判的核心对象。
creators.role_zh: 计算机科学家；普林斯顿大学副教授

creators.name: Abeba Birhane
creators.role: Cognitive scientist; Assistant Professor, Trinity College Dublin
creators.bio: Abeba Birhane is an Ethiopian-born cognitive scientist who audits large-scale datasets and writes on relational ethics and AI.
creators.bio_zh: Abeba Birhane 是出生于埃塞俄比亚的认知科学家，审计大规模数据集，并从关系伦理角度研究 AI。
creators.why: Her audits showed that the image datasets vision models learn from contain slurs, non-consensual and harmful images.
creators.why_zh: 她的审计揭示了视觉模型所学习的图像数据集中含有侮辱性标签、未经同意的和有害的图像。
creators.role_zh: 认知科学家；都柏林圣三一学院助理教授

creators.name: Zach Blas
creators.role: Artist, filmmaker and writer; Associate Professor, University of Toronto
creators.bio: Zach Blas is an American artist whose films, installations and masks examine biometrics, prediction and the politics of technology from a queer perspective.
creators.why: His collective masks and face cages turned biometric face recognition into a public, bodily matter and gave critical AI art its vocabulary of 'informatic opacity'.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、电影人与写作者；多伦多大学副教授
creators.bio_zh: Zach Blas 是美国艺术家，以酷儿视角通过影像、装置与面具审视生物识别、预测技术与技术政治。
creators.why_zh: 他的集体面具与“面部牢笼”把人脸识别变成公共的、身体性的议题，也为批判性 AI 艺术提供了“信息不透明”这一概念。

creators.name: Heather Dewey-Hagborg
creators.bio: Heather Dewey-Hagborg is an American artist whose work deals with genetic surveillance, DNA phenotyping and the algorithms that turn biological traces into faces.
creators.why: She shows how machines claim to read identity from bodily data, and how much of a 'face' is a model's guess.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、生物黑客
creators.bio_zh: Heather Dewey-Hagborg 是美国艺术家，作品关注基因监控、DNA 表型推断，以及把生物痕迹变成人脸的算法。
creators.why_zh: 她揭示机器如何声称能从身体数据中读出身份，以及一张“脸”有多少只是模型的猜测。

creators.name: Kyle McDonald
creators.bio: Kyle McDonald is an American artist who works with computer vision, machine learning and open-source tools, often in collaboration with Lauren Lee McCarthy.
creators.why: His projects let people experience from the inside how face analysis and crowd surveillance see and sort them.
creators.role_zh: 以代码创作的艺术家
creators.bio_zh: Kyle McDonald 是美国艺术家，使用计算机视觉、机器学习与开源工具创作，常与 Lauren Lee McCarthy 合作。
creators.why_zh: 他的作品让人从内部体验人脸分析与人群监控如何观看并给人分类。

creators.name: Lauren Lee McCarthy
creators.role: Artist; Professor, UCLA Design Media Arts
creators.bio: Lauren Lee McCarthy is an American artist examining social relationships amid surveillance, automation and algorithmic living; she created p5.js.
creators.why: She performs as, with and against smart systems, making their gaze and their social rules felt in the body.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；加州大学洛杉矶分校设计与媒体艺术系教授
creators.bio_zh: Lauren Lee McCarthy 是美国艺术家，关注监控、自动化与算法生活中的社会关系；她创建了 p5.js。
creators.why_zh: 她扮演智能系统、与之合作或与之对抗，让人亲身感受到它们的凝视与社交规则。

creators.name: Rafael Lozano-Hemmer
creators.bio: Rafael Lozano-Hemmer is a Mexican-Canadian artist whose interactive installations use tracking, biometrics and surveillance systems in public and museum spaces.
creators.why: Since the early 1990s he has turned machine tracking and face recognition back on the public, making the watching apparatus itself the work.
creators.role_zh: 媒体艺术家；Antimodular Research 创始人
creators.bio_zh: Rafael Lozano-Hemmer 是墨西哥裔加拿大艺术家，其互动装置在公共空间和美术馆中使用追踪、生物识别与监控系统。
creators.why_zh: 自 1990 年代初起，他把机器追踪与人脸识别反转向观众，让观看装置本身成为作品。

creators.name: Krzysztof Wodiczko
creators.role: Artist; Professor in Residence, Harvard Graduate School of Design
creators.bio: Krzysztof Wodiczko is a Polish-born artist known for large public projections and instruments that give voice to marginalised people.
creators.why: His collaboration with Lozano-Hemmer brings his long critique of public space and surveillance to robotic, face-detecting cameras.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；哈佛大学设计研究生院驻院教授
creators.bio_zh: Krzysztof Wodiczko 是波兰出生的艺术家，以大型公共投影及为边缘群体发声的“工具”作品闻名。
creators.why_zh: 他与洛萨诺-亨默的合作，把他对公共空间与监控的长期批判带入会检测人脸的机器人摄像机。

creators.name: Dries Depoorter
creators.bio: Dries Depoorter is a Belgian artist who makes installations, apps and online projects about privacy, surveillance cameras and machine learning.
creators.why: His works run real computer-vision pipelines on public camera feeds, showing how easily open data and AI combine into surveillance.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家
creators.bio_zh: Dries Depoorter 是比利时艺术家，以装置、应用和网络项目探讨隐私、监控摄像头与机器学习。
creators.why_zh: 他把真实的计算机视觉流程接到公开摄像头上，显示开放数据与 AI 能多么轻易地组合成监控。

creators.name: Karen Palmer
creators.bio: Karen Palmer is a British artist who makes immersive films that respond to the viewer's emotions and gaze through AI, eye tracking and facial analysis.
creators.why: She puts the viewer inside biased perception systems, so that their own face and fear steer the story.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家，自称“来自未来的讲故事者”
creators.bio_zh: Karen Palmer 是英国艺术家，创作通过 AI、眼动追踪与面部分析回应观众情绪与视线的沉浸式电影。
creators.why_zh: 她把观众放进带有偏见的感知系统之中，让观众自己的面孔与恐惧来推动剧情。

creators.name: Paolo Cirio
creators.bio: Paolo Cirio is an Italian artist whose interventions expose the legal, social and economic systems of information technology, from privacy to finance.
creators.why: He turns surveillance tools on the powerful, testing the asymmetry of who may be seen and identified by machines.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家
creators.bio_zh: Paolo Cirio 是意大利艺术家，其介入式作品揭示信息技术背后的法律、社会与经济系统，从隐私到金融。
creators.why_zh: 他把监控工具对准掌权者，检验“谁可以被机器看见和识别”这种不对称。

creators.name: Coralie Vogelaar
creators.bio: Coralie Vogelaar is a Dutch visual artist who works with emotion-recognition software, biofeedback and choreography to study how machines decode bodies.
creators.why: She stages the Facial Action Coding System as a score, showing how emotion AI reduces feeling to measurable muscle units.
creators.role_zh: 视觉艺术家
creators.bio_zh: Coralie Vogelaar 是荷兰视觉艺术家，结合情绪识别软件、生物反馈与编舞，研究机器如何解码身体。
creators.why_zh: 她把面部动作编码系统当作乐谱来演出，揭示情绪 AI 如何把感受简化为可测量的肌肉单元。

creators.name: Julien Prévieux
creators.bio: Julien Prévieux is a French artist whose films, performances and drawings examine how bodies and gestures are measured, patented and optimised by technical systems.
creators.why: His choreographies re-enact the protocols that made human movement machine-readable, from chronophotography to tracking software.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家；2014 年马塞尔·杜尚奖得主
creators.bio_zh: Julien Prévieux 是法国艺术家，以影像、表演与绘画研究身体与姿势如何被技术系统测量、申请专利与优化。
creators.why_zh: 他的编舞重演那些让人类动作变得可被机器读取的实验规程，从连续摄影到追踪软件。

creators.name: Lisa Feldman Barrett
creators.role: Psychologist and neuroscientist; University Distinguished Professor, Northeastern University
creators.bio: Lisa Feldman Barrett is a Canadian-American psychologist known for the theory of constructed emotion.
creators.why: Her team's review showed that facial movements do not reliably reveal emotions, undercutting the premise of emotion-recognition AI.
creators.role_zh: 心理学家、神经科学家；美国东北大学校级杰出教授
creators.bio_zh: Lisa Feldman Barrett 是加拿大裔美国心理学家，以“情绪建构论”闻名。
creators.why_zh: 她团队的综述表明，面部动作并不能可靠地揭示情绪，动摇了情绪识别 AI 的前提。

creators.name: Blaise Agüera y Arcas
creators.role: Engineer and researcher; VP and Fellow, Google
creators.bio: Blaise Agüera y Arcas is an American computer scientist who leads research on machine intelligence at Google and founded its Artists + Machine Intelligence programme.
creators.why: With Margaret Mitchell and Alexander Todorov he wrote an influential critique of machine-learning physiognomy.
creators.role_zh: 工程师与研究者；Google 副总裁、Fellow
creators.bio_zh: Blaise Agüera y Arcas 是美国计算机科学家，在 Google 领导机器智能研究，并创立了 Artists + Machine Intelligence 项目。
creators.why_zh: 他与 Margaret Mitchell、Alexander Todorov 合写的文章，是对机器学习“面相学”影响深远的批判。

creators.name: Adam Harvey
creators.role: Artist and researcher (computer vision, privacy, surveillance)
creators.bio: American artist and researcher who has worked on computer vision, biometrics and counter-surveillance since his 2010 NYU ITP thesis CV Dazzle. His later research projects trace how face datasets are built and apply object detection to human-rights archives.
creators.why: Turned face detection into a design problem and showed how everyday photos became training data for biometric surveillance.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、研究者（计算机视觉、隐私与监控）
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家、研究者，自 2010 年在纽约大学 ITP 的毕业作品 CV Dazzle 起持续研究计算机视觉、生物识别与反监控。后续研究追踪人脸数据集如何建成，并把目标检测技术用于人权档案。
creators.why_zh: 把“躲避人脸检测”变成设计问题，并揭示日常照片如何变成生物识别监控的训练数据。

creators.name: Jules LaPlace
creators.bio: Artist and programmer who built the website and search engine of MegaPixels and Exposing.ai with Adam Harvey.
creators.why: Co-built the search tool that lets people check whether their photos sit inside face-recognition datasets.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、软件开发者
creators.bio_zh: 艺术家、程序员，与 Adam Harvey 合作开发了 MegaPixels 与 Exposing.ai 的网站和搜索引擎。
creators.why_zh: 共同打造了让普通人查询自己的照片是否被收入人脸识别数据集的搜索工具。

creators.name: Sterling Crispin
creators.bio: American artist and technologist whose early work reverse-engineered face detection and recognition systems; he later worked on AR/VR and neurotechnology.
creators.why: Data-masks give physical form to what a face-recognition algorithm takes a face to be.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、技术专家
creators.bio_zh: 美国艺术家、技术专家，早期作品对人脸检测与识别系统进行逆向工程，后来从事 AR/VR 与神经技术研发。
creators.why_zh: Data-masks 把人脸识别算法心目中的“脸”做成了实体。

creators.name: Leo Selvaggio
creators.bio: Chicago-based interdisciplinary artist (Leonardo Selvaggio) whose projects on surveillance ask the public to wear, perform or hack his identity.
creators.why: URME Surveillance answers face recognition by multiplying one face instead of hiding many.
creators.role_zh: 跨领域艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 常驻芝加哥的跨领域艺术家（Leonardo Selvaggio），他关于监控的项目邀请公众佩戴、扮演或“黑入”他的身份。
creators.why_zh: URME Surveillance 对付人脸识别的办法不是隐藏许多张脸，而是复制同一张脸。

creators.name: Cap_able
creators.bio: Italian start-up founded by Rachele Didero and Federica Busani that makes knitwear with adversarial patterns against AI person and face detection; the idea began in New York in 2019.
creators.why: Brought adversarial examples out of the lab and into knitted clothing sold to the public.
creators.role_zh: 时尚科技初创公司（Rachele Didero、Federica Busani）
creators.bio_zh: 由 Rachele Didero 与 Federica Busani 创立的意大利初创公司，生产带有对抗图案、可干扰 AI 人体与人脸检测的针织服装；构想始于 2019 年的纽约。
creators.why_zh: 把对抗样本从实验室带进了可以买到、穿上的针织衣物。

creators.name: Tom White
creators.role: Artist (dribnet); Senior Lecturer, Victoria University of Wellington School of Design
creators.bio: New Zealand-based artist and design lecturer, known online as dribnet, who makes drawings and prints optimised to be read by neural-network classifiers.
creators.why: Makes art whose first audience is the machine, exposing how classifiers see abstract form.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家（dribnet）；惠灵顿维多利亚大学设计学院高级讲师
creators.bio_zh: 常驻新西兰的艺术家与设计讲师，网名 dribnet，创作专门供神经网络分类器“阅读”的绘画与版画。
creators.why_zh: 他的作品首先是给机器看的，从而暴露分类器如何理解抽象形状。

creators.name: James Bridle
creators.bio: British artist and writer on technology, networks and non-human intelligence, author of New Dark Age (2018) and Ways of Being (2022).
creators.why: Uses simple, ritual-like gestures to show how automated systems read and misread the world.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、作家
creators.bio_zh: 英国艺术家、作家，关注技术、网络与非人智能，著有《New Dark Age》（2018）和《Ways of Being》（2022）。
creators.why_zh: 用近乎仪式的简单动作，揭示自动化系统如何读取、又如何误读世界。

creators.name: Simon Weckert
creators.bio: Berlin-based artist whose performances and installations probe the social effects of digital technologies and platforms.
creators.why: Showed with a handcart of phones how a platform's sensing of the city can be fooled and then shapes real traffic.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家
creators.bio_zh: 常驻柏林的艺术家，以表演和装置探讨数字技术与平台的社会影响。
creators.why_zh: 用一辆装满手机的手推车证明：平台对城市的“感知”可以被欺骗，而这种错误又会改变真实的交通。

creators.name: Tomo Kihara
creators.role: Designer and artist; co-founder of Playfool
creators.bio: Japanese designer and artist who makes playful games and installations about AI, platforms and the city, often with Daniel Coppen as the studio Playfool.
creators.why: Turns the blind spots of machine perception into games the public can play and learn from.
creators.role_zh: 设计师、艺术家；Playfool 联合创始人
creators.bio_zh: 日本设计师、艺术家，常与 Daniel Coppen 以工作室 Playfool 的名义，创作关于 AI、平台与城市的游戏和装置。
creators.why_zh: 把机器感知的盲区变成公众可以亲手玩、从中学习的游戏。

creators.name: Daniel Coppen
creators.bio: British designer who co-founded the design studio Playfool with Tomo Kihara, making games and interactive installations.
creators.why: Co-created a street game that lets people test and expose pedestrian detection.
creators.role_zh: 设计师；Playfool 联合创始人
creators.bio_zh: 英国设计师，与木原共共同创立设计工作室 Playfool，创作游戏与互动装置。
creators.why_zh: 共同创作了一款让人亲身测试并揭露行人检测缺陷的街头游戏。

creators.name: Evolving AI Lab
creators.role: Research lab (Jeff Clune), University of Wyoming
creators.bio: Jeff Clune's lab at the University of Wyoming, working on evolutionary algorithms and deep learning; its members Anh Nguyen and Jason Yosinski co-authored the 'fooling images' paper.
creators.why: Showed that image classifiers confidently see objects in noise and abstract patterns that mean nothing to humans.
creators.role_zh: 研究实验室（Jeff Clune），怀俄明大学
creators.bio_zh: Jeff Clune 在怀俄明大学领导的实验室，研究进化算法与深度学习；成员 Anh Nguyen 与 Jason Yosinski 合著了“欺骗图像”论文。
creators.why_zh: 证明图像分类器会在噪声和对人类毫无意义的抽象图案中，自信地“看到”物体。

creators.name: Mahmood Sharif
creators.role: Computer security researcher; Tel Aviv University (PhD, Carnegie Mellon University)
creators.bio: Security and machine-learning researcher who, as a PhD student at Carnegie Mellon, led the study showing that printed eyeglass frames can fool face recognition.
creators.why: His adversarial glasses made physical evasion of face recognition concrete and wearable.
creators.role_zh: 计算机安全研究者；特拉维夫大学（卡内基梅隆大学博士）
creators.bio_zh: 安全与机器学习研究者，在卡内基梅隆大学读博期间主导了用打印眼镜框欺骗人脸识别的研究。
creators.why_zh: 他的对抗眼镜让“在现实中躲避人脸识别”变得具体、可以戴在脸上。

creators.name: Tom B. Brown
creators.role: Machine-learning researcher (Google Brain, later OpenAI and Anthropic)
creators.bio: Machine-learning researcher who led the 2017 Google Brain paper on the adversarial patch and later led work on large language models.
creators.why: The adversarial patch showed that a printed sticker can override everything else a classifier sees.
creators.role_zh: 机器学习研究者（Google Brain，后任职 OpenAI 与 Anthropic）
creators.bio_zh: 机器学习研究者，2017 年主导了 Google Brain 关于“对抗补丁”的论文，后来参与领导大语言模型研究。
creators.why_zh: 对抗补丁证明：一张打印贴纸就能压倒分类器看到的其他一切。

creators.name: Kevin Eykholt
creators.role: Computer security researcher (PhD, University of Michigan)
creators.bio: Security researcher who, at the University of Michigan, was first author of the study on stickers that make classifiers misread stop signs.
creators.why: His stop-sign experiment made the risks of adversarial examples for self-driving cars widely visible.
creators.role_zh: 计算机安全研究者（密歇根大学博士）
creators.bio_zh: 安全研究者，在密歇根大学期间作为第一作者发表了用贴纸让分类器误读停车标志的研究。
creators.why_zh: 他的停车标志实验让对抗样本对自动驾驶的风险广为人知。

creators.name: Lawrence Abu Hamdan
creators.bio: Artist whose audio investigations of voices, gunshots and silences have served as evidence in asylum hearings and human-rights cases; joint winner of the 2019 Turner Prize.
creators.why: He shows how listening becomes a technology of the border and the court: accent analysis, voice-stress lie detection and audio forensics that decide who is believed.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、声音调查者（自称“私人耳朵”）
creators.bio_zh: 艺术家，他对声音、枪声与沉默所做的音频调查曾在庇护听证和人权案件中被用作证据；2019 年特纳奖联合得主。
creators.why_zh: 他揭示“听”如何成为边境与法庭的技术：口音分析、语音测谎与音频取证，决定了谁的话会被相信。

creators.name: Machine Listening (Sean Dockray, James Parker, Joel Stern)
creators.bio: Platform for collaborative research and artistic experimentation founded in 2020 by Sean Dockray, James Parker and Joel Stern, working across writing, installation, performance, radio, software and pedagogy.
creators.why: They made 'machine listening' a critical field for art: voice assistants, audio datasets and acoustic surveillance treated as knowledge-power, extraction and control.
creators.role_zh: 研究与艺术团体
creators.bio_zh: 由 Sean Dockray、James Parker 与 Joel Stern 于 2020 年创立的协作研究与艺术实验平台，横跨写作、装置、表演、电台、软件与教学。
creators.why_zh: 他们把“机器聆听”变成艺术的批判领域：语音助手、音频数据集与声学监控被视为知识权力、攫取与控制。

creators.name: Kelly Dobson
creators.role: Artist and engineer; MIT Media Lab (Computing Culture group) alumna
creators.bio: Artist and engineer who built voice- and breath-driven machines at the MIT Media Lab, framing her practice as 'machine therapy'.
creators.why: Her domestic machines invert voice control: to make a machine listen you must sound like it, which turns interaction into empathy with an appliance.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、工程师；毕业于 MIT 媒体实验室（计算文化组）
creators.bio_zh: 艺术家与工程师，在 MIT 媒体实验室制作由声音和呼吸驱动的机器，并把自己的实践称为“机器疗法”。
creators.why_zh: 她的家用机器反转了语音控制：要让机器听你，你得先发出像它一样的声音，交互于是变成与电器的共情。

creators.name: Pedro Oliveira
creators.role: Sound artist and researcher; guest faculty, Sound Studies and Sonic Arts, Universität der Künste Berlin
creators.bio: Brazilian sound artist and researcher (born 1985, São Paulo) whose work examines how listening shapes and is shaped by technical infrastructures, focusing on voice and migration; founding member of Decolonising Design.
creators.why: He is the key artist on dialect-recognition software in the German asylum system, reading machine listening as colonial listening.
creators.role_zh: 声音艺术家、研究者；柏林艺术大学声音研究与声音艺术客座教师
creators.bio_zh: 巴西声音艺术家与研究者（1985 年生于圣保罗），研究“听”如何塑造技术基础设施又被其塑造，关注声音与移民；Decolonising Design 创始成员之一。
creators.why_zh: 他是研究德国庇护体系中“方言识别软件”的关键艺术家，把机器聆听解读为一种殖民式的聆听。

creators.name: Hito Steyerl
creators.bio: German artist, filmmaker and essayist (born 1966, Munich) whose videos and texts, from 'In Defense of the Poor Image' to 'Mean Images', analyse images, data and power in digital capitalism.
creators.why: She gives machine vision and AI a critical vocabulary: resolution as a regime of visibility, apophenia in pattern recognition, and the statistical 'mean image'.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、电影人、写作者
creators.bio_zh: 德国艺术家、电影人与散文作者（1966 年生于慕尼黑），从《为贫乏影像辩护》到《平均图像》，她的影像与文章分析数字资本主义中的图像、数据与权力。
creators.why_zh: 她为机器视觉与 AI 提供了批判词汇：分辨率作为可见性的制度、模式识别中的“幻想性错觉”、以及统计出来的“平均图像”。

creators.name: Bjørn Karmann
creators.bio: Danish designer trained at the Copenhagen Institute of Interaction Design (CIID) who builds working devices that let people train, hack or rethink machine perception.
creators.why: His objects make machine senses tangible and negotiable: a parasite that deafens smart speakers, a socket you teach by example, a camera that sees through data instead of light.
creators.role_zh: 设计师、创意技术专家
creators.bio_zh: 丹麦设计师，毕业于哥本哈根交互设计学院（CIID），制作可以实际运行的设备，让人训练、改造或重新思考机器感知。
creators.why_zh: 他的物件让机器的感官变得可触摸、可协商：让智能音箱“失聪”的寄生装置、靠示范来教会的插座、以数据而非光线来“看”的相机。

creators.name: Tore Knudsen
creators.bio: Danish interaction designer and CIID alumnus working on tangible interfaces for machine learning and smart-home technology.
creators.why: Co-author of Project Alias, a key example of a user-built counter-device against always-listening voice assistants.
creators.role_zh: 交互设计师、研究者
creators.bio_zh: 丹麦交互设计师，CIID 校友，研究面向机器学习与智能家居的实体交互界面。
creators.why_zh: Project Alias 的共同作者；这件作品是用户自制、对抗“永远在听”的语音助手的典型反设备。

creators.name: Joana Moll
creators.bio: Barcelona-based artist and researcher whose works examine the material, ecological and surveillant infrastructures of the internet, from border webcams to data brokers and the carbon cost of websites.
creators.why: She exposes what networked machines actually record and consume, often by letting their own automated outputs speak.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、研究者
creators.bio_zh: 常驻巴塞罗那的艺术家与研究者，作品考察互联网的物质、生态与监控基础设施，从边境摄像头到数据经纪商，再到网站的碳排放。
creators.why_zh: 她常让联网机器自己的自动产出发声，揭示它们实际记录和消耗了什么。

creators.name: Nicholas Carlini
creators.bio: Computer-security researcher known for foundational work on adversarial examples, audio adversarial attacks and training-data extraction from neural networks.
creators.why: His attacks show that speech recognisers hear things humans cannot, and can be commanded by sounds that are noise to us.
creators.role_zh: 机器学习安全研究者
creators.bio_zh: 计算机安全研究者，以对抗样本、音频对抗攻击以及从神经网络中提取训练数据的奠基性研究闻名。
creators.why_zh: 他的攻击表明，语音识别器能“听到”人听不到的东西，也能被对人来说只是噪声的声音所操控。

creators.name: Allison Koenecke
creators.role: Computational social scientist; Assistant Professor of Information Science, Cornell University
creators.bio: Researcher in algorithmic fairness who led the first large audit of racial disparities in commercial speech recognition.
creators.why: Her audit gave hard numbers to the claim that listening machines hear some voices worse than others.
creators.role_zh: 计算社会科学家；康奈尔大学信息科学助理教授
creators.bio_zh: 算法公平研究者，主导了第一项针对商用语音识别种族差异的大规模审计。
creators.why_zh: 她的审计用确切数据证明：听觉机器对某些人的声音“听”得更差。

creators.name: Brian House
creators.bio: Artist working with sound, data and environmental sensing, whose projects turn tracking, listening and infrastructure into perceptible rhythms.
creators.why: With Kyle McDonald he made Conversnitch, which shows the human labour and publicity hidden behind an eavesdropping device.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、研究者
creators.bio_zh: 以声音、数据与环境感测为媒介的艺术家，把追踪、聆听与基础设施转化为可感知的节奏。
creators.why_zh: 他与 Kyle McDonald 合作的 Conversnitch 揭示了窃听设备背后隐藏的人工劳动与公开化。

creators.name: Johann Diedrick
creators.role: Artist and engineer; adjunct professor, NYU ITP
creators.bio: Artist and engineer who makes 'listening rooms' through installations, performances, software and workshops, and teaches sound art and listening machines at NYU ITP; 2021 Mozilla Creative Media Award recipient.
creators.why: He brings Black speech and its absence from training data to the centre of machine-listening art.
creators.role_zh: 艺术家、工程师；纽约大学 ITP 兼职教授
creators.bio_zh: 艺术家与工程师，通过装置、表演、软件与工作坊营造“聆听空间”，在纽约大学 ITP 教授声音艺术与聆听机器；2021 年 Mozilla 创意媒体奖得主。
creators.why_zh: 他把黑人的语音，以及它在训练数据中的缺席，放到了机器聆听艺术的中心。

creators.name: Wesley Goatley
creators.role: Critical artist and researcher; Reader in Technology Futures & Critical Climate Computing, University of the Arts London
creators.bio: Artist and researcher whose installations and audio fictions interrogate voice assistants, the AI industry and the climate cost of computation.
creators.why: His works stage smart speakers as listening objects to be listened to, exposing what voice assistants hear, hide and cannot answer.
creators.role_zh: 批判艺术家、研究者；伦敦艺术大学技术未来与批判气候计算高级讲师
creators.bio_zh: 艺术家与研究者，他的装置与声音虚构作品追问语音助手、AI 产业与计算的气候成本。
creators.why_zh: 他把智能音箱当作需要被“反过来聆听”的对象，揭示语音助手听到了什么、藏起了什么、又回答不了什么。

works.title: Eye/Machine I–III
works.description: A three-part video installation (2001–03) that assembles footage from missile-head cameras, industrial robots and computer-vision research, images that no human was meant to watch.
works.description_zh: 三部曲录像装置（2001–03），汇集导弹弹头摄像机、工业机器人与计算机视觉研究中的影像，这些图像本不是给人看的。
works.idea_en: Once images become part of an operation rather than a picture of it, seeing turns into targeting, sorting and control.
works.idea_zh: 当图像成为操作的一部分，而不再是对操作的描绘，“看”就变成了瞄准、分拣与控制。
works.method: Double-projection montage of found military, industrial and laboratory footage (smart bombs, welding robots, object recognition), with guidance lines and overlays drawn by the machines themselves.
works.method_zh: 以双屏投影剪辑军事、工业和实验室的现成影像（智能炸弹、焊接机器人、物体识别），画面上保留机器自己绘制的引导线与叠加标记。

works.title: Deep Play
works.description: A 12-channel installation that replays the 2006 World Cup final through TV feeds, surveillance cameras, player-tracking software and animated data graphics, all running in sync.
works.description_zh: 一件 12 频道装置，以电视信号、监控摄像头、球员追踪软件和动画数据图同步重放 2006 年世界杯决赛。
works.idea_en: The same match becomes many different images once machines watch it: a spectacle for fans, a dataset for coaches, a crowd for the police.
works.idea_zh: 同一场比赛一旦由机器来看，就分裂成许多种图像：对球迷是奇观，对教练是数据，对警察是人群。
works.method: Twelve synchronised video tracks of 2 h 15 min combine the broadcast clean feed, security-camera footage and computer-generated tracking and statistics of every player.
works.method_zh: 12 条各长 2 小时 15 分钟的同步影像，结合转播原始信号、安保摄像画面，以及对每名球员的计算机追踪与统计。

works.title: Sight Machine
works.description: The Kronos Quartet plays live while cameras feed a suite of computer-vision algorithms; what the machines 'see' in the musicians is projected on a screen behind them.
works.description_zh: Kronos Quartet 现场演奏，摄像头把画面输入一组计算机视觉算法，机器在乐手身上“看到”的内容实时投影在他们身后。
works.idea_en: A concert watched by machines shows how little of music, gesture and feeling survives in a machine's description of people.
works.idea_zh: 一场被机器观看的音乐会表明：在机器对人的描述里，音乐、姿态与情感几乎荡然无存。
works.method: Live camera feeds pass through face detection, object recognition, pose and other vision algorithms whose outputs are rendered and projected in real time during the performance.
works.method_zh: 现场摄像画面经过人脸检测、物体识别、姿态估计等视觉算法处理，结果在演出中实时渲染并投影。

works.title: It Began as a Military Experiment
works.description: Ten portraits chosen from FERET, the DARPA-funded face database of the 1990s built largely from staff at a military base in Maryland, printed with the keypoints a face-recognition algorithm finds.
works.description_zh: 从 FERET 数据库中挑选的十张肖像。FERET 是 1990 年代由 DARPA 资助的人脸库，照片主要来自马里兰一处军事基地的人员；作品同时印出人脸识别算法找到的关键点。
works.idea_en: Face recognition was built on the faces of particular people, the 'Adam and Eves' of a technology they never chose to found.
works.idea_zh: 人脸识别建立在一些具体的人脸之上：他们成了这项技术的“亚当与夏娃”，却从未选择过这个身份。
works.method: Months of curating the FERET database, retouching and colour-correcting selected images, then running them through a facial-landmark algorithm; set of 10 pigment prints.
works.method_zh: 花数月从 FERET 数据库中挑选、修图并校色，再用人脸关键点算法处理；共 10 张颜料打印作品。

works.title: Machine Readable Hito
works.description: A wall of hundreds of portraits of the artist Hito Steyerl, each captioned with what facial-analysis algorithms guess about her age, gender, emotion, glasses or beard.
works.description_zh: 由数百张艺术家 Hito Steyerl 肖像组成的墙面，每张下方标注人脸分析算法对她年龄、性别、情绪、是否戴眼镜或有胡须的猜测。
works.idea_en: Facial analysis turns a known person into columns of confident guesses that contradict each other from one image to the next.
works.idea_zh: 人脸分析把一个熟悉的人变成一列列自信的猜测，而这些猜测在每张图之间彼此矛盾。
works.method: Hundreds of photographs run through several commercial and open-source facial-analysis classifiers; outputs printed under each image on adhesive wall material.
works.method_zh: 数百张照片经多个商业与开源人脸分析分类器处理，结果印在每张图下方，以墙贴材料呈现。

works.title: Behold These Glorious Times!
works.description: A 10-minute video that alternates training images used to teach AI to recognise objects, faces and emotions with the grids of features a deep neural network extracts from them, set to music by Holly Herndon.
works.description_zh: 一部 10 分钟的录像：交替呈现用来教 AI 识别物体、人脸与情绪的训练图像，以及深度神经网络从中提取的特征网格，配乐由 Holly Herndon 创作。
works.idea_en: We rarely see what a network sees; here the images that teach machines and the machine's own decomposition of them share one screen.
works.idea_zh: 我们很少看到网络“看见”的东西；这里，用来教机器的图像和机器对它们的拆解出现在同一块屏幕上。
works.method: Training-library images are fed through a convolutional network and its intermediate activations are visualised; the score was made partly with neural voice synthesis and speech-recognition training data.
works.method_zh: 把训练库中的图像输入卷积网络并可视化其中间激活；配乐部分使用了神经网络语音合成与语音识别训练数据。

works.title: From ‘Apple’ to ‘Anomaly’ (Pictures and Labels)
works.description: About 30,000 printed photographs from the ImageNet dataset line the Barbican's curved gallery, grouped under their labels, moving from harmless nouns like 'apple' to judgments about people.
works.description_zh: 约三万张来自 ImageNet 数据集的照片按标签分组，铺满巴比肯中心弧形展厅，从“苹果”这样无害的名词逐渐走向对人的评判。
works.idea_en: A training set is a worldview: walking along its labels shows how quickly naming things slides into judging people.
works.idea_zh: 训练数据集就是一种世界观：沿着它的标签走下去，会看到命名事物如何迅速滑向评判他人。
works.method: Selection of ImageNet categories and images printed individually and pinned in label clusters along the 90-metre Curve wall; a homage to Magritte's The Treachery of Images.
works.method_zh: 从 ImageNet 中选取类别与图像，逐张打印，按标签成簇钉在 90 米长的弧形墙上，向马格利特《图像的背叛》致敬。

works.title: They Took the Faces from the Accused and the Dead… (SD18)
works.description: A grid of thousands of mugshots from NIST Special Database 18, a set of arrest photographs, many of people now dead, supplied to researchers to develop and test face recognition.
works.description_zh: 由数千张嫌犯照片组成的网格，来自美国国家标准与技术研究院的 Special Database 18：这些逮捕照片（其中许多人已经去世）被提供给研究者，用于开发和测试人脸识别。
works.idea_en: Face recognition was benchmarked on people who could not consent: the accused, the imprisoned and the dead.
works.idea_zh: 人脸识别的基准测试建立在无法表示同意的人身上：被指控者、被关押者与死者。
works.method: Images drawn from the NIST mugshot database used as a research benchmark, printed as pigment prints and as a large wall installation.
works.method_zh: 取自 NIST 嫌犯照片数据库（一个研究基准数据集），以颜料打印和大型墙面装置呈现。
exhibited: Uncanny Valley, de Young Museum, San Francisco, 2020

works.title: ImageNet Roulette
works.description: A web app and installation that labelled anyone's selfie using a model trained on ImageNet's 'person' categories, returning terms that were often absurd, racist or cruel; millions of people tried it in September 2019.
works.description_zh: 一个网页应用兼装置，用基于 ImageNet“人”类别训练的模型给任何人的自拍贴标签，返回的词常常荒谬、带种族歧视或残忍；2019 年 9 月有数百万人试用。
works.idea_en: Letting the training set 'speak for itself' showed that classifying people by appearance is harmful by design, not by accident.
works.idea_zh: 让训练数据集“自己说话”，揭示了按外貌给人分类在设计上就有害，而非偶然出错。
works.method: A classifier trained on ImageNet's roughly 2,800 person sub-categories detected faces and returned the nearest label; the online version was withdrawn and continues as the installation Faces of ImageNet (2022).
works.method_zh: 在 ImageNet 约 2800 个“人”子类别上训练的分类器检测人脸并返回最接近的标签；网上版本已下线，作为装置《Faces of ImageNet》（2022）延续。
exhibited: Poetics of Encryption, Kunsthal Charlottenborg, 2024 (as Faces of ImageNet)
The World Through AI, Jeu de Paume, Paris, 2025 (as Faces of ImageNet)

works.title: Training Humans
works.description: An exhibition of the photographs used to train computer vision to recognise people, from early government-funded face databases such as FERET to images scraped from the web and sets built for emotion recognition.
works.description_zh: 一场展出用来训练计算机视觉“认人”的照片的展览，从 FERET 等早期政府资助的人脸数据库，到从网络上抓取的图像和为情绪识别构建的数据集。
works.idea_en: Training images are a vernacular photography nobody looks at, yet they decide how machines will see everyone.
works.idea_zh: 训练图像是一种无人观看的日常摄影，却决定了机器将如何看待每一个人。
works.method: Curated display of historical and current training datasets (faces, gestures, emotions, gait) as prints and wall grids, with ImageNet Roulette as an interactive piece.
works.method_zh: 以打印作品和墙面网格策展呈现历史与当代的训练数据集（人脸、手势、情绪、步态），并以《ImageNet Roulette》作为互动作品。

works.title: Excavating AI: The Politics of Images in Machine Learning Training Sets
works.description: An essay that digs through ImageNet, JAFFE, UTKFace and other training sets layer by layer, from their taxonomies and categories down to individual labelled images.
works.description_zh: 一篇文章，逐层挖掘 ImageNet、JAFFE、UTKFace 等训练数据集，从分类体系、类别一直深入到单张被贴上标签的图像。
works.idea_en: Every training set encodes a politics: deciding what an image means is an act of power, never neutral description.
works.idea_zh: 每个训练数据集都编码了一种政治：决定一张图像“是什么”是权力的行使，而不是中立的描述。
works.method: Archaeological reading of dataset structure (WordNet hierarchy, label choices, sourcing) with image examples; published online by the authors with the AI Now Institute.
works.method_zh: 以考古式方法解读数据集结构（WordNet 层级、标签选择、图像来源），配以图像实例；由作者与 AI Now 研究所在线发表。

paper.title: Excavating AI: The Politics of Images in Machine Learning Training Sets

works.title: Learning to See
works.description: A camera looks at everyday objects on a table (cables, keys, cloth) and neural networks trained only on waves, fire, clouds or flowers redraw them in real time as seascapes and skies.
works.description_zh: 摄像头对着桌上的日常物件（电线、钥匙、布料），只在海浪、火焰、云或花上训练过的神经网络实时把它们重绘成海景和天空。
works.idea_en: A network can only see through what it already knows, and so can we.
works.idea_zh: 神经网络只能透过它已知的东西去看，人也一样。
works.method: Custom image-to-image networks (pix2pix-style) trained on single-theme datasets reconstruct a live camera feed of the table as an interactive installation and a series of videos.
works.method_zh: 在单一主题数据集上训练的定制图像到图像网络（类似 pix2pix）重建桌面的实时摄像画面，形式包括互动装置与系列录像。
exhibited: AI: More than Human, Barbican, London, 2019
Understanding AI, Ars Electronica Center, Linz

works.title: Computers Watching Movies
works.description: A computer vision system watches six famous film scenes (2001, American Beauty, Inception, Taxi Driver, The Matrix, Annie Hall) and its gaze is drawn as moving sketch lines over black, synced to the original audio.
works.description_zh: 一个计算机视觉系统观看六部名片的片段（《2001 太空漫游》《美国丽人》《盗梦空间》《出租车司机》《黑客帝国》《安妮·霍尔》），它的视线以移动的线条画在黑底上，并与原片音轨同步。
works.idea_en: A machine without our narrative habits looks at different things than we do, which exposes how culturally trained our own looking is.
works.idea_zh: 没有人类叙事习惯的机器会看向不同的地方，这反过来暴露了人类的观看有多么受文化训练。
works.method: Custom software using computer-vision and AI routines decides where to look in each frame; the traces are rendered as temporal sketches (computationally produced HD video).
works.method_zh: 艺术家编写的软件用计算机视觉与 AI 程序决定每一帧看向哪里，轨迹被渲染成随时间展开的素描（计算生成的高清录像）。

works.title: The Giver of Names
works.description: Visitors place any object on an empty pedestal; a camera captures it, the computer analyses its outline, colour and texture, and then speaks aloud a poetic, often odd, sentence naming it.
works.description_zh: 观众把任意物品放在空基座上；摄像头捕捉画面，计算机分析其轮廓、颜色与纹理，然后大声说出一句诗意而常常古怪的话来为它命名。
works.idea_en: Machine naming works by association, not understanding; its misreadings show perception as a chain of guesses.
works.idea_zh: 机器命名靠联想而非理解；它的误读显示，感知其实是一串猜测。
works.method: Video camera and image processing (outline, segmentation, colour and texture analysis) feed an associative database of words and ideas that generates a grammatical sentence, voiced by speech synthesis.
works.method_zh: 摄像头与图像处理（轮廓、分割、颜色与纹理分析）驱动一个由词语与概念组成的联想数据库，生成合乎语法的句子并用语音合成说出。
exhibited: Kiasma Museum of Contemporary Art, Helsinki (commission)

works.title: Sorting Daemon
works.description: A robotic camera scans the street outside the gallery for people, cuts each passer-by out of the background and breaks them into colour patches, which are sorted by hue into a large projected composite.
works.description_zh: 一台机器人摄像头扫描展厅外的街道寻找行人，把每个路人从背景中抠出并拆成色块，再按色相排列成一幅巨大的投影拼贴。
works.idea_en: Automated profiling does not see people, only features it can sort; the painterly composite is a portrait of that reduction.
works.idea_zh: 自动化画像看不见人，只看见可以分类的特征；那幅如绘画般的拼贴正是这种化约的肖像。
works.method: Pan-tilt-zoom camera with motion detection and background subtraction; extracted figures are segmented by colour and placed by hue, saturation and size (flesh tones sorted separately).
works.method_zh: 云台变焦摄像头配合运动检测与背景差分；被提取的人物按颜色分割，再依色相、饱和度与大小排列（肤色单独归类）。

works.title: Videoplace
works.description: Participants' live video silhouettes appear on a large screen where the computer recognises their outlines and lets them touch, draw with and play with graphic creatures and remote participants.
works.description_zh: 参与者的实时视频剪影出现在大屏幕上，计算机识别他们的轮廓，让他们触碰、绘画，并与图形生物及远方参与者互动。
works.idea_en: Long before webcams, the computer perceived the whole body, and the body learned to act for the machine's eye.
works.idea_zh: 早在网络摄像头出现之前，计算机就已感知整个身体，而身体也学会了为机器之眼而动作。
works.method: Video cameras, custom hardware for real-time silhouette extraction and contour analysis, and projected computer graphics; shown in a two-way version at the Milwaukee Art Museum in 1975.
works.method_zh: 摄像机、实时提取剪影与分析轮廓的定制硬件，以及投影计算机图形；1975 年在密尔沃基美术馆以双向版本展出。

works.title: The Nine Eyes of Google Street View
works.description: An ongoing collection of screenshots from Google Street View, where the nine-lens camera cars have recorded arrests, accidents, animals and odd moments without anyone looking.
works.description_zh: 一个持续进行的 Google 街景截图合集：九镜头拍摄车在无人注视时记录下逮捕、事故、动物和各种奇怪瞬间。
works.idea_en: An indifferent automated camera produces a new kind of photograph: nobody chose the moment, yet it still says something about the world.
works.idea_zh: 漠然的自动相机产生了一种新的摄影：没有人选择按快门的时刻，但照片仍在诉说世界。
works.method: Screen captures selected by the artist from Street View imagery, shown online, as prints and in books.
works.method_zh: 由艺术家从街景图像中挑选截图，以网站、打印作品和书籍形式呈现。

works.title: Postcards from Google Earth
works.description: Screenshots from Google Earth of bridges melting into rivers and highways draped over hills, sold as postcards on postcard racks.
works.description_zh: Google Earth 截图：桥梁融化进河流，高速公路像布料一样披在山坡上；作品以明信片形式陈列在明信片架上出售。
works.idea_en: These are not glitches but the system working as designed: Google Earth is a database disguised as a photograph.
works.idea_zh: 这些不是故障，而是系统按设计运行的结果：Google Earth 是一个伪装成照片的数据库。
works.method: Unmanipulated screenshots where aerial photographs are texture-mapped onto a 3D terrain model that knows nothing about bridges; printed as inkjet postcards and shown on a website.
works.method_zh: 未经修改的截图：航拍照片被贴图到一个并不知道桥梁存在的三维地形模型上；以喷墨明信片和网站呈现。

works.title: False Positives
works.description: Photographs of Brussels' business district, composed from a CCTV vantage point, each staging one of eight 'anomalies' that intelligent surveillance systems are trained to flag, such as standing still or looking back repeatedly.
works.description_zh: 从监控摄像头的高视角拍摄布鲁塞尔商务区，每幅作品演绎智能监控系统被训练去标记的八种“异常”之一，例如静止不动或反复回头。
works.idea_en: Behavioural detection makes ordinary gestures suspicious; to be 'normal' is to move the way the algorithm expects.
works.idea_zh: 行为检测让日常动作变得可疑；所谓“正常”，就是按算法预期的方式移动。
works.method: Digital composites of several photographs per scene, based on eight anomalies identified with surveillance experts (standing still, fast movements, lonely objects, corner placement, clusters breaking apart, synchronised movements, repeatedly looking back, deviant directions).
works.method_zh: 每个场景由多张照片数字合成，依据与监控专家一起归纳的八种异常（静止、快速移动、孤立物品、停在角落、人群散开、同步动作、反复回头、逆向行走）。
exhibited: Resistant Faces, Pinakothek der Moderne, Munich, 2021

works.title: Words That Remake the World «The Seeker»
works.description: The Seeker, an AI entity, watched the world through millions of insecure security cameras and named what it saw; its descriptions became a huge drawing and whispering robot avatars (CKRBT, 2019).
works.description_zh: AI 实体 The Seeker 通过数以百万计的不设防监控摄像头观看世界，并为所见之物命名；这些描述变成一幅巨大的绘图，以及会低语的机器人化身 CKRBT（2019）。
works.idea_en: When machines describe the world through surveillance cameras, they begin to write a vocabulary of the world made for and by machines.
works.idea_zh: 当机器通过监控摄像头描述世界时，它们开始写下一套由机器生成、也为机器服务的世界词汇。
works.method: Custom software harvested frames from unsecured internet cameras and sent them to cloud image-recognition services; labels and confidence scores were logged, mapped and spoken by synthesised voices.
works.method_zh: 定制软件从未加密的网络摄像头抓取画面并发送到云端图像识别服务，标签与置信度被记录、绘制成图，并由合成语音说出。

works.title: Pique Nique pour les Inconnues
works.description: The anonymous women on colour test cards (Lena, Shirley and others), along with bots and stock-photo placeholders, gather on a desktop and try to sing together using only computer system sounds.
works.description_zh: 色彩测试卡上的无名女性（Lena、Shirley 等），连同聊天机器人和图库占位图，聚集在电脑桌面上，试图只用系统提示音一起合唱。
works.idea_en: The standards by which machines see images were calibrated on women whose faces survive endless copying while their names disappear.
works.idea_zh: 机器观看图像的标准是用女性面孔校准的：她们的脸在无尽复制中留存，名字却消失了。
works.method: Desktop video 'tele-chorale' animating historical test images and virtual assistants, voiced with operating-system sounds performing Paul McCartney's 'We All Stand Together'.
works.method_zh: 以桌面录像形式呈现的“远程合唱”，让历史测试图像与虚拟助手动起来，用操作系统声音演唱 Paul McCartney 的《We All Stand Together》。

works.title: Lacework
works.description: A slow, dreamlike video river made from MIT's Moments in Time dataset: one million three-second clips scraped from the web and each tagged with a single verb such as 'praying' or 'flying'. Pipkin watched the whole dataset and stretched its clips into hallucinatory slow motion.
works.description_zh: 一条由 MIT「Moments in Time」数据集构成的缓慢、梦境般的影像之河：数据集含一百万段从网络抓取的三秒短片，每段只被标注一个动词，如“祈祷”“飞”。Pipkin 看完了整个数据集，并把这些片段拉伸成幻觉般的慢动作。
works.idea_en: A training set is made of other people's lives, reduced to one word each; watching it all restores their weight.
works.idea_zh: 训练集由他人的生活片段组成，每段只剩一个词；把它完整看一遍，才重新感到这些生活的分量。
works.method: Clips from the Moments in Time action-recognition dataset were processed with neural frame interpolation and super-resolution to slow and enlarge them into a continuous video.
works.method_zh: 用神经网络插帧与超分辨率算法处理「Moments in Time」动作识别数据集中的片段，将其放慢、放大，连成一段连续影像。
exhibited: The Photographers' Gallery, London (Data / Set / Match), 2020

works.title: Myriad (Tulips)
works.description: An installation of thousands of photographs of tulips that Ridler bought, photographed and labelled by hand over one tulip season; the images became the training set for her GAN work Mosaic Virus. Each print carries her handwritten label.
works.description_zh: 一件由数千张郁金香照片组成的装置：Ridler 在一个郁金香花季里亲自购买、拍摄并手写标注每一朵花，这些图像随后成为她的 GAN 作品《Mosaic Virus》的训练集。每张照片上都留着她手写的标签。
works.idea_en: Showing the dataset instead of the model reveals the slow human labour and judgement on which machine learning rests.
works.idea_zh: 展示数据集而非模型，揭示了机器学习所依赖的缓慢人工劳动与人的判断。
works.method: About 10,000 tulip photographs taken and hand-annotated by the artist, displayed as prints with handwritten labels; the set was later used to train a GAN.
works.method_zh: 艺术家亲自拍摄并手工标注约一万张郁金香照片，以带手写标签的照片形式展出；该数据集后来用于训练 GAN。
exhibited: AI: More than Human, Barbican, London, 2019

works.title: Declassifier (Humans of AI)
works.description: A computer-vision program looks at photographs, but instead of drawing boxes around the objects it detects, it overlays the actual COCO training images that taught it to see each object. Part of Humans of AI, which also credits the thousands of Flickr photographers whose pictures built the dataset.
works.description_zh: 一个计算机视觉程序在观看照片，但它不在识别出的物体周围画框，而是叠加上当初教会它认出这些物体的 COCO 训练图像。作品属于《Humans of AI》系列，该系列还为构成数据集的数千位 Flickr 摄影师署名。
works.idea_en: Every act of machine recognition is a recollection of someone else's photographs.
works.idea_zh: 机器的每一次“认出”，都是对别人照片的一次回忆。
works.method: An object detector trained on Microsoft's COCO dataset processes images; for each detection the software retrieves and collages the COCO training photos of that class, with photographer credits.
works.method_zh: 用在微软 COCO 数据集上训练的物体检测器处理图像；每检测到一个物体，软件就调出并拼贴该类别的 COCO 训练照片，并注明摄影师。

works.title: Computed Curation
works.description: A 29-metre leporello photobook sequenced entirely by a computer: vision algorithms tag, caption and arrange the artist's photographs by content and composition. The odd captions and links invite readers to guess the machine's logic.
works.description_zh: 一本长达 29 米的折页摄影书，照片顺序完全由计算机决定：视觉算法按内容与构图为艺术家的照片打标签、写说明并排序。那些古怪的说明与关联，引导读者去揣测机器的逻辑。
works.idea_en: Letting a machine edit a photobook teaches readers to see through the eyes of an algorithm, including its blind spots.
works.idea_zh: 让机器来编辑摄影书，读者便学会用算法的眼睛看世界，也看见它的盲点。
works.method: Image-recognition services generate tags and captions while a layout algorithm links photos by visual and semantic similarity; printed as a leporello and web version.
works.method_zh: 图像识别服务生成标签与说明，排版算法按视觉与语义相似度把照片串联起来；以折页书和网页版呈现。
exhibited: DAAD Art Show, German Consulate New York, 2018

works.title: Segmentation.Network
works.description: A website that plays back more than 600,000 outlines drawn by crowd-workers around objects in Flickr photos for Microsoft's COCO dataset. Line by line, it shows the hand work that decides what machines can see.
works.description_zh: 一个网站，逐一回放众包工人为微软 COCO 数据集在 Flickr 照片中勾画的 60 多万条物体轮廓。一笔一笔地，它展示了决定机器“能看见什么”的手工劳动。
works.idea_en: Machine vision is drawn by hand: someone decided where each object ends and what stays unrecognised.
works.idea_zh: 机器视觉是手绘出来的：有人决定了每个物体的边界，也决定了什么将不被识别。
works.method: Custom software animates the polygon segmentation annotations of the COCO dataset in sequence; also shown as a projection (2018).
works.method_zh: 定制软件按顺序动画回放 COCO 数据集中的多边形分割标注；2018 年另有投影装置版本。

works.title: This is the Problem, the Solution, the Past and the Future
works.description: A conceptual training dataset of 2,931 photographs from The Photographers' Gallery website, sorted by almost 30,000 visitor clicks into four categories: Problem, Solution, Past and Future. The clicks were collected in Schmieg's intervention Decision Space (2016), which overlaid the gallery's site with these four buttons.
works.description_zh: 一个概念性的训练数据集：摄影师画廊网站上的 2931 张照片，经访客近三万次点击，被分入“问题、解决方案、过去、未来”四类。这些点击来自 Schmieg 2016 年的介入作品《Decision Space》，它在画廊网站的每张图上都加了这四个按钮。
works.idea_en: Any category can be taught to a machine once enough people click; the absurd labels expose how arbitrary all labels are.
works.idea_zh: 只要有足够多的人点击，任何类别都能教给机器；荒诞的标签暴露出所有标签的任意性。
works.method: A web intervention collected crowd classifications of gallery images; the resulting labelled dataset was published online and as wallpaper, and used to train an image classifier (Decisive Camera).
works.method_zh: 通过网页介入收集公众对画廊图像的分类；由此得到的标注数据集以网站和墙纸形式发布，并用于训练图像分类器（《Decisive Camera》）。
exhibited: Commissioned by The Photographers' Gallery, London, 2016–17

works.title: The Normalizing Machine
works.description: Visitors are recorded and then asked to point at the person who looks 'most normal' in a line-up of earlier participants. The machine aggregates these choices into an algorithmic image of normality, echoing Alphonse Bertillon's 19th-century 'speaking portrait'.
works.description_zh: 观众先被拍下面孔，再从之前参与者的列队中指出看起来“最正常”的人。机器把这些选择汇总成一幅算法化的“正常”肖像，呼应 19 世纪 Alphonse Bertillon 的“口述肖像”体系。
works.idea_en: Algorithmic prejudice is built from our own small judgements, collected and hidden inside a black box.
works.idea_zh: 算法偏见由我们自己的细小判断汇聚而成，再被藏进黑箱。
works.method: A camera records each participant; their pointing choices label previous faces, and a machine-learning model aggregates the votes into a map of facial 'normality' (software by Dan Stavy and Eran Weissenstern, openFrameworks).
works.method_zh: 摄像头记录每位参与者；他们的指认为先前的面孔打上标签，机器学习模型把投票汇总成“面部正常度”的分布（软件由 Dan Stavy 与 Eran Weissenstern 以 openFrameworks 开发）。
exhibited: BIAS: Built This Way, Science Gallery Dublin, 2021

works.title: Triple-Chaser
works.description: Made for the 2019 Whitney Biennial, the film traces Triple-Chaser tear-gas grenades fired at civilians back to Safariland, a company owned by Whitney vice-chair Warren B. Kanders. Because few real photographs existed, the team trained classifiers on photorealistic synthetic images to search for the grenades online.
works.description_zh: 为 2019 年惠特尼双年展而作。影片追踪向平民发射的 Triple-Chaser 催泪弹，追溯到惠特尼美术馆董事会副主席 Warren B. Kanders 所拥有的 Safariland 公司。由于真实照片极少，团队用逼真的合成图像训练分类器，在网络上搜寻这种弹药。
works.idea_en: Computer vision can be turned against power: a machine taught with synthetic images becomes a witness to state violence.
works.idea_zh: 计算机视觉可以反过来对抗权力：用合成图像教出来的机器，成为国家暴力的证人。
works.method: 3D models of the grenade were rendered into thousands of synthetic training images with varied lighting and backgrounds, used to train machine-learning classifiers that scan online imagery; film made with Praxis Films.
works.method_zh: 把催泪弹的三维模型渲染成数千张光照和背景各异的合成训练图像，用来训练扫描网络图像的机器学习分类器；影片与 Praxis Films 合作完成。

works.title: Model Zoo
works.description: A growing catalogue of 3D models of munitions and weapons, together with the machine-learning classifiers trained on synthetic renderings of them to recognise these objects in images from conflicts.
works.description_zh: 一个不断扩充的目录：收录弹药与武器的三维模型，以及用这些模型的合成渲染图训练、用于在冲突影像中识别它们的机器学习分类器。
works.idea_en: Where real images of violence are scarce, synthetic training sets let machines learn to see what investigators need to find.
works.idea_zh: 当暴力的真实影像稀缺时，合成训练集让机器学会看见调查者需要找到的东西。
works.method: Photorealistic renderings of 3D weapon models form synthetic datasets; classifiers trained on them are tested on open-source footage.
works.method_zh: 以武器三维模型的逼真渲染图组成合成数据集；在其上训练的分类器再用开源影像进行检验。

works.title: HOMESCHOOL
works.description: A 13-minute 3D-animated film set inside the synthetic model homes used to train the computer vision of household robots. It asks how thousands of homes, people's most private spaces, are turned into categories a robot can navigate: is this a vase, a bowl or a cup?
works.description_zh: 一部 13 分钟的三维动画影片，场景设在用于训练家用机器人计算机视觉的合成样板房里。它追问：成千上万个家，人们最私密的空间，如何被变成机器人可以导航的类别——这是花瓶、碗还是杯子？
works.idea_en: Before a robot can live in your home, the home must be rebuilt as a dataset, and whatever does not fit a category disappears.
works.idea_zh: 机器人住进你家之前，家必须先被重建为数据集；凡是不合类别的东西都会消失。
works.method: 3D animation built from assets and floor plans of synthetic indoor training datasets for domestic robot vision, with a four-channel soundtrack.
works.method_zh: 用家用机器人视觉所用的合成室内训练数据集中的模型与平面图制作三维动画，配四声道声音。
exhibited: Commissioned by Housing the Human, with Swissnex San Francisco and Fotomuseum Winterthur, 2019

works.title: Sorting Song
works.description: Domestic objects from the SceneNet RGB-D training dataset morph endlessly between vase and bowl, bench and couch, chair and toilet. When shape is all a dataset records, a wheelchair, a toilet and an electric chair can end up in the same category.
works.description_zh: 来自 SceneNet RGB-D 训练数据集的家居物品在花瓶与碗、长凳与沙发、椅子与马桶之间不断变形。当数据集只记录形状时，轮椅、马桶和电椅可能被归入同一类。
works.idea_en: Object categories that seem trivial to people are negotiations the machine cannot have; the boundary between bowl and vase is a political choice.
works.idea_zh: 对人来说理所当然的物品类别，是机器无法参与的协商；碗与花瓶的边界其实是一种选择。
works.method: 3D meshes from Imperial College London's SceneNet RGB-D indoor dataset are animated morphing between category labels.
works.method_zh: 把帝国理工学院 SceneNet RGB-D 室内数据集中的三维网格制成在不同类别标签之间变形的动画。

works.title: Salaf (Ancestors)
works.description: Tracing her family's migrations across Arabia and Mesopotamia, the artist ran archival photographs, many from Gertrude Bell's colonial archive, through computer-vision models. They failed to see veiled women as women and tagged Bedouin as 'soldier' and 'army'; she then erased the figures to make an 'absent dataset' of about 6,000 images.
works.description_zh: 艺术家追溯家族穿越阿拉伯半岛与美索不达米亚的迁徙，把大量档案照片（许多来自 Gertrude Bell 的殖民档案）输入计算机视觉模型。模型认不出戴面纱的女性是女性，还把贝都因人标为“士兵”“军队”；于是她用分割算法抹去其中的人物，制成约 6000 张图像的“缺席数据集”。
works.idea_en: Machine vision inherits the colonial archive: to refuse its gaze, the artist trains on absence.
works.idea_zh: 机器视觉继承了殖民档案的目光；为了拒绝这种目光，艺术家用“缺席”来训练机器。
works.method: Scraped museum and archival photographs were labelled by commercial computer-vision models; an AI segmentation technique then removed the orientalist figures to create an empty-image dataset.
works.method_zh: 用商用计算机视觉模型为抓取的博物馆与档案照片打标签，再用 AI 分割技术移除其中带东方主义色彩的人物，生成“空图像”数据集。

works.title: Zizi – Queering the Dataset
works.description: A multi-channel video of faces in constant transition, generated after a face model trained on 70,000 photographs was retrained with 1,000 images of drag and gender-fluid faces. The network's weights drift away from the normative faces it learned first.
works.description_zh: 一件多频道影像，画面中的面孔不断变换：一个用七万张照片训练的人脸模型，再加入一千张变装与性别流动者的面孔重新训练后生成了这些图像。网络的权重逐渐偏离它最初学到的“规范”面孔。
works.idea_en: Adding the faces a dataset left out shifts what the machine can imagine, and shows what it had not learned.
works.idea_zh: 把数据集遗漏的面孔加进去，机器能想象的范围就会改变，也暴露出它原本没学到什么。
works.method: StyleGAN trained on the FFHQ face dataset was fine-tuned with about 1,000 drag and gender-fluid faces found online; the latent space is traversed to make a 135-minute loop.
works.method_zh: 在 FFHQ 人脸数据集上训练的 StyleGAN，再用网上找到的约一千张变装与性别流动者面孔微调；在潜空间中游走，生成 135 分钟的循环影像。
exhibited: You and AI, Onassis Foundation, Athens, 2021
Among the Machines, Zabludowicz Collection, London, 2022

works.title: Membrane
works.description: A fixed camera watches a Berlin street while a neural network learns its patterns and generates new image sequences from them. Visitors use an interface to steer which learned features the network recombines, watching analysis turn into invention.
works.description_zh: 一台固定摄像机注视着柏林的一条街道，神经网络学习其中的模式，并由此生成新的影像序列。观众通过界面引导网络重新组合哪些已学到的特征，看着分析如何变成虚构。
works.idea_en: A seeing machine does not record the street; it remembers features and reassembles them into a street of its own.
works.idea_zh: 会看的机器并不记录街道；它记住特征，再把它们重组为属于自己的街道。
works.method: Live video from a street camera trains a Temporal GAN (TGAN, extended with wavelets) that generates new sequences; an interface lets visitors choose image features.
works.method_zh: 街头摄像机的实时影像用于训练时序生成对抗网络（TGAN，并加入小波扩展）来生成新序列；观众通过界面选择图像特征。

works.title: ImageNet: A Large-Scale Hierarchical Image Database
works.description: The CVPR 2009 paper by Jia Deng, Wei Dong, Richard Socher, Li-Jia Li, Kai Li and Li Fei-Fei introducing ImageNet: millions of web images sorted into the noun hierarchy of WordNet and verified by crowd-workers on Amazon Mechanical Turk. It became the benchmark that launched deep-learning computer vision.
works.description_zh: 邓嘉、董伟、Richard Socher、李李佳、李凯与李飞飞在 CVPR 2009 发表的论文，推出 ImageNet：数百万张网络图像按 WordNet 名词层级分类，并由亚马逊 Mechanical Turk 众包工人核验。它成为开启深度学习计算机视觉的基准。
works.idea_en: A machine's way of seeing is inherited from a dictionary's hierarchy of nouns and from thousands of anonymous clicks.
works.idea_zh: 机器看世界的方式，继承自一部词典的名词层级和成千上万次匿名点击。
works.method: Images were collected by querying search engines with WordNet synonym sets, then cleaned and verified by Amazon Mechanical Turk workers.
works.method_zh: 以 WordNet 同义词集检索搜索引擎收集图像，再由亚马逊 Mechanical Turk 工人清洗和核验。

paper.title: ImageNet: A large-scale hierarchical image database

works.title: Large Image Datasets: A Pyrrhic Win for Computer Vision?
works.description: Abeba Birhane and Vinay Uday Prabhu audited large image datasets, including ImageNet and MIT's 80 Million Tiny Images, and found slurs among the labels and non-consensual, pornographic and harmful images. The paper led MIT to withdraw Tiny Images.
works.description_zh: Abeba Birhane 与 Vinay Uday Prabhu 审计了 ImageNet、MIT「8000 万张微型图像」等大型图像数据集，发现标签中有侮辱性词汇，并含有未经同意的、色情的和有害的图像。这篇论文促使 MIT 撤下了 Tiny Images 数据集。
works.idea_en: What a vision model can see depends on images collected without consent and labels no one checked.
works.idea_zh: 视觉模型能看见什么，取决于未经同意收集的图像和无人核查的标签。
works.method: A quantitative and qualitative audit of labels and image content in large-scale vision datasets, with proposed remedies.
works.method_zh: 对大规模视觉数据集的标签与图像内容进行定量与定性审计，并提出改进建议。

paper.title: Large image datasets: A pyrrhic win for computer vision?

works.title: Facial Weaponization Suite
works.description: Blas runs community workshops where participants' faces are scanned and merged into amorphous, colourful collective masks that face recognition cannot read. The masks are worn in public actions and in the video 'Facial Weaponization Communiqué: Fag Face'.
works.description_zh: Blas 组织社区工作坊，扫描参与者的面孔并把数据融合成无定形、色彩鲜艳的“集体面具”，人脸识别无法读取它们。面具被用于公共行动，也出现在影片《Facial Weaponization Communiqué: Fag Face》中。
works.idea_en: Opacity can be collective: a face that belongs to many people is a face the machine cannot identify.
works.idea_zh: 不透明可以是集体的：一张属于许多人的脸，是机器无法识别的脸。
works.method: Participants' faces are 3D-scanned, the biometric data are aggregated in modelling software and the combined forms are fabricated as wearable masks; the Fag Face Mask answers studies claiming to detect sexual orientation from faces.
works.method_zh: 参与者的面部被三维扫描，生物特征数据在建模软件中聚合，再制成可佩戴的面具；其中“Fag Face Mask”回应了声称可从面孔判断性取向的研究。
exhibited: Workshops and public actions in Los Angeles, San Diego, New York and Mexico City, 2012–14

works.title: Face Cages
works.description: Four queer artists each wear a metal cage built from the biometric diagram of their own face, enduring it on camera until the pain shows. The four-channel video sets the clean geometry of face recognition against the discomfort of the body it measures.
works.description_zh: 四位酷儿艺术家各自戴上由自己面部生物识别图形制成的金属笼，在镜头前忍耐到疼痛显露。四频道影像把人脸识别干净的几何图形与被测量身体的不适并置。
works.idea_en: Biometric diagrams look abstract and neutral; made in steel and worn, they become a cage.
works.idea_zh: 生物识别图形看起来抽象而中立；一旦用钢铁做出来戴在脸上，它就是一只牢笼。
works.method: Facial-recognition landmark diagrams of each performer were generated and 3D-printed in stainless steel, then worn in endurance performances filmed as a four-channel HD video (12 min).
works.method_zh: 为每位表演者生成人脸识别的特征点图形，以不锈钢 3D 打印，然后在耐力表演中佩戴，拍成四频道高清影像（12 分钟）。

works.title: Stranger Visions
works.description: Dewey-Hagborg collected hairs, chewed gum and cigarette butts from New York streets, extracted DNA and computed life-size, full-colour 3D-printed portraits of what the strangers might look like. The masks hang beside the sample and where it was found.
works.description_zh: Dewey-Hagborg 在纽约街头收集头发、嚼过的口香糖和烟头，提取 DNA，计算并 3D 打印出这些陌生人“可能长相”的真人大小彩色肖像，与样本及其发现地点一同展出。
works.idea_en: A face predicted from data is a statistical guess presented as a likeness, and the guess is already a form of surveillance.
works.idea_zh: 从数据预测出的面孔，是被当作肖像呈现的统计猜测，而这种猜测本身已是一种监控。
works.method: DNA was extracted and sequenced at a community biolab; SNPs linked to ancestry, sex, eye and hair colour fed custom software that set parameters of a 3D face model, printed in full colour.
works.method_zh: 在社区生物实验室提取并测序 DNA；与祖源、性别、眼睛和头发颜色相关的 SNP 输入自编软件，设定三维人脸模型的参数，再彩色打印成型。

works.title: Probably Chelsea
works.description: Thirty different 3D-printed faces hang in a crowd, all generated by algorithms from the same DNA: cheek swabs and hair that Chelsea Manning mailed from prison. Made with Manning to mark her release in 2017.
works.description_zh: 三十张不同的 3D 打印面孔悬挂成人群，全部由算法根据同一份 DNA 生成：Chelsea Manning 从狱中寄出的口腔拭子与头发。作品与 Manning 合作完成，庆祝她 2017 年获释。
works.idea_en: One genome yields thirty plausible faces: DNA does not determine a face, and identity cannot be read off the body.
works.idea_zh: 一份基因组生成三十张可能的脸：DNA 并不决定一张脸，身份也无法从身体上直接读出。
works.method: Manning's DNA was analysed with forensic phenotyping methods; varying the algorithm's interpretations of the same genetic data produced 30 face models, 3D-printed in colour.
works.method_zh: 用法医表型推断方法分析 Manning 的 DNA；改变算法对同一基因数据的解读，得到 30 个面孔模型，彩色 3D 打印。

works.title: us+
works.description: A Google Hangout app that listens to and watches a video call, scoring each speaker's words and facial expressions and popping up advice such as 'stop talking about yourself'; if the conversation gets out of balance, it mutes someone automatically.
works.description_zh: 一个 Google Hangout 应用，在视频通话中聆听并观察双方，为每个人的用词和面部表情打分，弹出“别再谈你自己了”之类的建议；对话失衡时会自动把某人静音。
works.idea_en: When software reads our faces and words to improve a conversation, it also decides what a good conversation is.
works.idea_zh: 当软件通过读取我们的表情和话语来“改善”对话时，它也在决定什么才算好的对话。
works.method: Audio, facial-expression and linguistic analysis based on the LIWC word database and Linguistic Style Matching drive live visualisations, notifications and auto-muting inside Google Hangouts.
works.method_zh: 基于 LIWC 词库与“语言风格匹配”理论的音频、面部表情与语言分析，驱动 Google Hangouts 中的实时可视化、提醒与自动静音。

works.title: Vibe Check
works.description: Cameras in the exhibition use face recognition and expression analysis to log what emotions each visitor provokes in others. A screen at the entrance names the people who cause the most happiness, disgust, sadness, surprise or boredom, and visitors may find themselves listed on the way out.
works.description_zh: 展厅中的摄像头用人脸识别与表情分析记录每位观众在他人脸上引发的情绪。入口的屏幕列出最能引起快乐、厌恶、悲伤、惊讶或无聊的人，观众离开时可能发现自己也上了榜。
works.idea_en: Emotion recognition turns every encounter into a score, and the gallery becomes a small social-credit system.
works.idea_zh: 情绪识别把每一次相遇变成分数，展厅变成了一个小型社会信用系统。
works.method: Off-the-shelf face recognition and expression classifiers track visitors across cameras, attribute the expressions of nearby people to whoever they are looking at, and publish the rankings on screens.
works.method_zh: 现成的人脸识别与表情分类器在多个摄像头之间追踪观众，把旁人的表情归因于他们正注视的人，并在屏幕上公布排名。
exhibited: Real Feelings, HEK Basel 2020 (commissioned by HEK and MU)

works.title: Unlearning Language
works.description: Up to eight people are guided by an AI that 'wants to train humans to be less machine-like': whenever it detects their speech, gestures or expressions it intervenes with light, sound and vibration, so the group has to invent ways of communicating it cannot detect, such as humming, clapping or shifting pitch.
works.description_zh: 最多八位参与者由一个“想训练人类不那么像机器”的 AI 引导：一旦它检测到他们的语音、手势或表情，就用光、声音和振动加以干预，于是大家必须发明它检测不到的交流方式，比如哼唱、拍手或改变音高。
works.idea_en: Evading machine perception becomes a way of rediscovering what is most human in how we communicate.
works.idea_zh: 躲避机器感知，成了重新发现人类交流中最“人性”部分的方法。
works.method: Speech detection, gesture recognition and expression detection run on cameras and microphones in the room and trigger light, sound and haptic feedback; made with the Yamaguchi Center for Arts and Media.
works.method_zh: 房间中的摄像头与麦克风运行语音检测、手势识别与表情检测，并触发灯光、声音与触觉反馈；与山口情报艺术中心（YCAM）合作完成。
exhibited: Yamaguchi Center for Arts and Media (YCAM) 2022

works.title: Facework
works.description: A browser game set in a gig economy where face analysis is the job: as a 'Faceworker', the player takes gigs that require the webcam to judge them as, say, wearing glasses or looking happy, and learns in real time how the classifier sees and where it fails.
works.description_zh: 一个设定在“零工经济”中的网页游戏，面部分析就是工作：玩家作为“Faceworker”接单，任务要求摄像头判定你戴着眼镜或看起来很开心，玩家由此实时体会分类器如何观看，又在哪里失灵。
works.idea_en: Playing to a face classifier builds an intuition for seeing like a machine, and for how arbitrary its categories are.
works.idea_zh: 迎合人脸分类器的游戏过程，让人建立起“像机器一样看”的直觉，也看清它的类别有多随意。
works.method: In-browser face-attribute classifiers run on the player's webcam; gig tasks are scored live against their outputs. Supported by the Mozilla Foundation.
works.method_zh: 浏览器内的人脸属性分类器在玩家的摄像头上运行，每项零工任务都依据其输出实时打分。由 Mozilla 基金会资助。

works.title: Exhausting a Crowd
works.description: Twelve hours of Piccadilly Circus filmed from above become a website where anyone can pause, zoom and attach notes to any person in the crowd. After Georges Perec's 'An Attempt at Exhausting a Place in Paris', it shows what crowd-sourced, annotating surveillance looks like.
works.description_zh: 在高处拍下的皮卡迪利广场十二小时影像被做成网站，任何人都可以暂停、放大，并给人群中任意一个人加注释。作品取自 Georges Perec《穷尽巴黎某地的尝试》，呈现“众包标注式监控”的样子。
works.idea_en: Surveillance footage becomes a dataset the moment people start labelling it; the crowd does the machine's watching.
works.idea_zh: 当人们开始给监控画面打标签，它就变成了数据集；是人群在替机器观看。
works.method: A 4K camera recorded 3 pm to 3 am from a building on Piccadilly Circus; a custom web player stores time-coded, spatial annotations from online visitors. Made with Jonas Jongejan.
works.method_zh: 4K 摄像机从皮卡迪利广场一栋建筑上连续拍摄下午 3 点至凌晨 3 点；定制网页播放器保存线上访客带时间码和位置的标注。与 Jonas Jongejan 合作。
exhibited: All of This Belongs to You, V&A London 2015

works.title: Level of Confidence
works.description: A face-recognition camera compares each visitor's face with the portraits of the 43 students abducted in Iguala, Mexico, in 2014, and shows which student they most resemble with a percentage of confidence. The match is never positive; the search does not stop.
works.description_zh: 一台人脸识别摄像机把每位观众的脸与 2014 年在墨西哥伊瓜拉被绑架的 43 名学生的肖像比对，显示观众最像哪一位学生及其“置信度”。匹配永远不会成功，搜寻也永不停止。
works.idea_en: A surveillance algorithm built to find suspects is turned into a tool of mourning that searches for victims.
works.idea_zh: 原本用来寻找嫌疑人的监控算法，被转为寻找受害者的哀悼工具。
works.method: Eigenface, Fisherface and LBPH face-recognition algorithms trained on the students' photographs run on a camera-and-screen unit; proceeds from sales go to the students' community.
works.method_zh: 以学生照片训练的 Eigenface、Fisherface 与 LBPH 人脸识别算法在摄像头与屏幕装置上运行；作品销售所得捐给学生所在的社区。

works.title: Zoom Pavilion
works.description: In a room surrounded by projections, twelve computerised surveillance systems detect visitors' faces and robotic cameras zoom in on them up to 35 times, cutting from crowd views to abstract close-ups and recording the spatial relationships between strangers.
works.description_zh: 在四周投影环绕的房间里，十二套计算机化监控系统检测观众的面孔，机器人摄像机把镜头放大到 35 倍，在人群全景与抽象特写之间切换，并记录陌生人之间的空间关系。
works.idea_en: Being picked out and enlarged by a face detector makes the ordinary experience of public surveillance suddenly personal.
works.idea_zh: 被人脸检测器挑出并放大，让公共监控这一日常经验突然变得私人。
works.method: Face detection software steers independent robotic PTZ cameras with up to 35x optical zoom, whose feeds are projected across the walls.
works.method_zh: 人脸检测软件驱动独立的机器人云台摄像机（最高 35 倍光学变焦），其画面投影在各面墙上。

works.title: Surface Tension
works.description: A giant human eye on a screen follows each visitor around the room with 'Orwellian precision'. Made during the first Gulf War, the first war of camera-guided 'intelligent' bombs, it gives the tracking machine an eye that looks back.
works.description_zh: 屏幕上一只巨大的人眼以“奥威尔式的精确”跟随每位观众在房间里移动。作品创作于第一次海湾战争期间，那是摄像头制导“智能”炸弹首次大规模使用的战争；它给追踪机器装上了一只会回看的眼睛。
works.idea_en: Machine tracking has a gaze: once it is given an eye, being followed by it feels like being watched by someone.
works.idea_zh: 机器追踪自有其凝视：一旦给它一只眼睛，被它跟随就像被某人注视。
works.method: A computerised tracking system detects the viewer's position and selects frames from over 500 stop-motion photographs of an eye so that it appears to follow them.
works.method_zh: 计算机追踪系统检测观众位置，从 500 多张眼睛的定格照片中选取画面，使眼睛看起来一直在追随观众。
exhibited: West Kowloon Cultural District, Hong Kong 2023

works.title: The Follower
works.description: Depoorter recorded open webcams in public squares for weeks, scraped Instagram photos tagged at those places, and used AI to find the exact moment each photo was taken: side-by-side clips show the posing influencer and the unseen camera watching.
works.description_zh: Depoorter 连续数周录制公共广场的开放网络摄像头，抓取在这些地点标记的 Instagram 照片，再用 AI 找出每张照片被拍下的确切瞬间：并排的片段一边是摆拍的网红，一边是无人注意的监视画面。
works.idea_en: Every staged photo has a second, unposed image taken by a machine, and AI can link the two.
works.idea_zh: 每张摆拍照片都有另一张由机器拍下的、不设防的图像，而 AI 能把两者连起来。
works.method: Weeks of footage from publicly accessible webcams were matched against scraped, location-tagged Instagram posts with image-similarity and person-detection software.
works.method_zh: 用图像相似度与人物检测软件，把公开网络摄像头数周的录像与抓取来的带地点标签的 Instagram 帖子逐一比对。

works.title: Jaywalking
works.description: Visitors watch live traffic webcams from around the world in which software flags pedestrians crossing on red; with one button they can send a screenshot of the offence to the nearest police station.
works.description_zh: 观众观看全球各地的实时交通摄像头，软件会标出闯红灯过马路的行人；只需按一个按钮，就能把违规截图发送到最近的警察局。
works.idea_en: Automated detection makes reporting effortless, and hands the visitor the moral weight of the machine's judgement.
works.idea_zh: 自动检测让举报变得毫不费力，也把机器判断的道德重量交到观众手里。
works.method: Live feeds from publicly accessible traffic cameras are analysed for pedestrians in the crossing during a red light; a button emails the captured frame to the local police.
works.method_zh: 分析公开交通摄像头的直播画面，找出红灯时位于人行横道上的行人；按下按钮即可把截取的画面通过电子邮件发送给当地警方。

works.title: The Flemish Scrollers
works.description: Software watches the Flemish Parliament's daily livestreams, detects when a politician is looking at their phone, identifies them by face and posts the clip on social media, tagging them by name.
works.description_zh: 软件监看弗拉芒议会每天的直播，一旦发现有议员低头看手机，就通过人脸识别认出其身份，把片段发到社交媒体并点名标记。
works.idea_en: Automated face recognition, usually aimed at citizens, is turned on the people who make the rules for it.
works.idea_zh: 通常对准公民的自动人脸识别，被转向为它制定规则的人。
works.method: Keras object-detection and face-recognition models analyse the parliament's YouTube livestreams; FFmpeg cuts clips that are posted automatically to Twitter and Instagram. Running since 5 July 2021.
works.method_zh: Keras 目标检测与人脸识别模型分析议会的 YouTube 直播；FFmpeg 剪出片段，自动发布到 Twitter 与 Instagram。自 2021 年 7 月 5 日起运行。

works.title: Perception iO
works.description: The viewer takes the point of view of a police officer's body camera in a tense encounter with a Black and a white protagonist; eye tracking and facial emotion analysis read the viewer's reactions, and the story branches according to their implicit bias.
works.description_zh: 观众以警察随身摄像头的视角进入一场紧张的遭遇，面对一位黑人和一位白人主角；眼动追踪与面部情绪分析读取观众反应，剧情按照观众的隐性偏见分岔。
works.idea_en: The installation reads the viewer the way a biased system reads a suspect, making them feel whose perception becomes consequence.
works.idea_zh: 作品像带偏见的系统读取嫌疑人那样读取观众，让人感受到谁的感知会变成后果。
works.method: Tobii eye tracking and AI facial-expression analysis (developed with ThoughtWorks Arts) feed a branching narrative film engine.
works.method_zh: Tobii 眼动追踪与 AI 面部表情分析（与 ThoughtWorks Arts 合作开发）驱动一套分支叙事电影引擎。
exhibited: Face Values, Cooper Hewitt, Smithsonian Design Museum, New York 2019–20
BIAS: Built This Way, Science Gallery Dublin 2021

works.title: Capture
works.description: Cirio ran 1,000 press photos of protests in France through face recognition, built a database of 4,000 police officers' faces and invited the public to identify them by name, and pasted the headshots as posters across Paris.
