France's interior minister demanded the work be censored.
works.description_zh: Cirio 用人脸识别处理了 1000 张法国抗议活动的新闻照片，建立了包含 4000 名警察面孔的数据库，邀请公众辨认他们的姓名，并把头像做成海报张贴在巴黎街头。法国内政部长要求审查这件作品。
works.idea_en: Face recognition feels different when it is pointed at the police: the outrage exposes the asymmetry of who may be identified.
works.idea_zh: 当人脸识别对准警察时，感觉就不一样了：由此引发的愤怒揭示了“谁可以被识别”的不对称。
works.method: Public photographs were processed with face-detection and recognition software to extract and cluster officers' faces, published on the platform Capture-Police.com and printed as street posters; linked to a campaign to ban facial recognition in Europe.
works.method_zh: 用人脸检测与识别软件处理公开照片，提取并聚类警察面孔，发布在 Capture-Police.com 平台上并印成街头海报；与“在欧洲禁止人脸识别”的倡议相连。

works.title: Random String of Emotions
works.description: An actress performs 200 facial expressions assembled from random combinations of Action Units, the muscle movements that emotion-recognition software uses, and commercial software then tries to name the emotion of each strange, sometimes impossible face.
works.description_zh: 一位演员表演由“动作单元”随机组合而成的 200 个面部表情——动作单元是情绪识别软件所用的肌肉运动单位——随后商业软件尝试为每张奇特、有时近乎不可能的脸命名情绪。
works.idea_en: Reversing emotion AI's decoding exposes how thin its vocabulary of six basic emotions is.
works.idea_zh: 把情绪 AI 的解码流程倒过来，暴露了它“六种基本情绪”的词汇有多单薄。
works.method: A computer generates random strings of FACS Action Units that the actress learns to perform; the filmed fragments are analysed live by Noldus FaceReader and shown on a second screen.
works.method_zh: 电脑随机生成 FACS 动作单元序列，由演员学习并表演；拍下的片段交给 Noldus FaceReader 分析，读数在第二块屏幕上显示。

works.title: Patterns of Life
works.description: Five dancers of the Paris Opera perform choreographies derived from scientific protocols that turned human movement into data, from Marey's chronophotography and Gilbreth's time-motion studies to point-light displays and today's tracking software. The title is the military term for analysing a target's habits from surveillance data.
works.description_zh: 五位巴黎歌剧院舞者表演源自科学实验规程的编舞，这些规程把人类动作变成数据：从马雷的连续摄影、吉尔布雷斯的动作研究，到光点显示与今天的追踪软件。片名来自军方用语，指从监控数据中分析目标的生活规律。
works.idea_en: Machine-readable movement has a history: every tracking system first taught bodies how to be measured.
works.idea_zh: 可被机器读取的动作有其历史：每一种追踪系统都先教会身体如何被测量。
works.method: A film shot in six settings in which the dancers re-enact historical and contemporary motion-capture and tracking experiments; co-produced by the Paris Opera's 3e Scène for Prévieux's Centre Pompidou show.
works.method_zh: 影片在六个场景中拍摄，舞者重演历史与当代的动作捕捉和追踪实验；由巴黎歌剧院 3e Scène 联合制作，用于普雷维厄在蓬皮杜中心的个展。
exhibited: Prix Marcel Duchamp 2014 exhibition, Centre Pompidou, Paris 2015–16

works.title: Emotional Expressions Reconsidered: Challenges to Inferring Emotion From Human Facial Movements
works.description: Barrett, Adolphs, Marsella, Martinez and Pollak review more than 1,000 studies and conclude that people do not reliably make the same facial movements for the same emotions across situations and cultures, so a scowl cannot be read as anger.
works.description_zh: Barrett、Adolphs、Marsella、Martinez 与 Pollak 综述了 1000 多项研究，结论是：在不同情境与文化中，人们并不会为同一种情绪可靠地做出相同的面部动作，所以皱眉不能被直接读成愤怒。
works.idea_en: Emotion-recognition AI detects facial movements, not feelings; the inference from one to the other is the weak link.
works.idea_zh: 情绪识别 AI 检测到的是面部动作，而非感受；从前者推断后者正是最薄弱的一环。
works.method: A systematic review of evidence on the reliability and specificity of facial configurations for anger, disgust, fear, happiness, sadness and surprise in adults, infants, children and remote cultures.
works.method_zh: 系统综述成人、婴儿、儿童及偏远文化群体中，愤怒、厌恶、恐惧、快乐、悲伤与惊讶等面部构型的可靠性与特异性证据。

paper.venue: Psychological Science in the Public Interest 20(1)
paper.title: Emotional Expressions Reconsidered: Challenges to Inferring Emotion From Human Facial Movements

works.title: Physiognomy's New Clothes
works.description: An essay by Blaise Agüera y Arcas, Margaret Mitchell and Alexander Todorov dissecting a 2016 paper that claimed deep learning could detect 'criminality' from ID photos, and tracing the idea back to Lombroso and nineteenth-century physiognomy.
works.description_zh: Blaise Agüera y Arcas、Margaret Mitchell 与 Alexander Todorov 合写的长文，剖析一篇 2016 年声称深度学习能从证件照中识别“犯罪性”的论文，并把这一想法追溯到龙勃罗梭与十九世纪的面相学。
works.idea_en: A classifier trained on biased photographs learns the bias and returns it as objective 'science'.
works.idea_zh: 用有偏见的照片训练出的分类器会学会这种偏见，再以客观“科学”的面目把它交还给我们。
works.method: A long-form critical essay combining machine-learning analysis of the claimed results (dataset differences such as expression and clothing) with the history of physiognomy and scientific racism.
works.method_zh: 一篇长篇批判文章，结合对所谓结果的机器学习分析（如数据集中表情、衣着的差异）与面相学和科学种族主义的历史。

works.title: CV Dazzle
works.description: A camouflage strategy of bold make-up and asymmetric hairstyles that breaks the features a face detector looks for, so the wearer stays visible to people but disappears for the algorithm.
works.description_zh: 一套由大胆妆容和不对称发型组成的伪装策略，打散人脸检测器寻找的特征：人仍然看得见佩戴者，算法却看不见。
works.idea_en: A face is whatever the detector's template says it is; designing against that template reveals it.
works.idea_zh: “脸”是检测器模板所规定的样子；针对模板去设计，就把模板暴露了出来。
works.method: Looks were designed and tested against the Viola-Jones Haar-cascade face detector in OpenCV (later looks, 2020, against CNN face recognition).
works.method_zh: 造型针对 OpenCV 中的 Viola-Jones Haar 级联人脸检测器设计并测试（2020 年的新造型则针对卷积神经网络人脸识别）。

works.title: Stealth Wear
works.description: An anti-drone hoodie, hijab and burqa made of silver-plated fabric that hides the wearer's body heat from overhead thermal cameras.
works.description_zh: 一组防无人机的连帽衫、头巾和罩袍，用镀银面料遮挡人体热量，让头顶的热成像相机看不到穿着者。
works.idea_en: When the machine sees in heat, privacy becomes a question of what your clothes radiate.
works.idea_zh: 当机器用热量去看，隐私就变成了衣服向外辐射什么的问题。
works.method: Garments are sewn from silver-plated synthetic fabric that reflects thermal radiation; they were tested with a FLIR thermal camera.
works.method_zh: 服装用能反射热辐射的镀银合成面料缝制，并用 FLIR 热成像相机测试。

works.title: HyperFace
works.description: A textile print covered with patterns that face detectors read as many false faces, so the real face nearby gets a lower confidence score.
works.description_zh: 一种布料印花，图案会被人脸检测器读成许多张“假脸”，从而降低旁边真实人脸的置信度。
works.idea_en: Instead of hiding a face, flood the machine with faces only it can see.
works.idea_zh: 与其藏起一张脸，不如让机器被只有它自己看得见的脸淹没。
works.method: Patterns were generated from what face-detection algorithms score as faces; developed with Hyphen-Labs for NeuroSpeculative AfroFeminism.
works.method_zh: 图案依据人脸检测算法判为“脸”的特征生成；与 Hyphen-Labs 合作，为 NeuroSpeculative AfroFeminism 项目开发。

works.title: MegaPixels / Exposing.ai
works.description: A research project and search engine that traces where face and biometric training datasets came from and lets anyone check whether their Flickr photos were used in them.
works.description_zh: 一个研究项目和搜索引擎，追溯人脸与生物识别训练数据集的来源，并让任何人查询自己的 Flickr 照片是否被收入其中。
works.idea_en: Face recognition is built from ordinary photos taken for other reasons; the dataset is where the surveillance begins.
works.idea_zh: 人脸识别建立在人们出于别的目的拍下的普通照片之上；监控始于数据集。
works.method: Photo IDs and metadata from dozens of public face datasets scraped from Flickr (2004–2020) are indexed so users can search them; MegaPixels ran 2017–2020 and was relaunched as Exposing.ai in 2021.
works.method_zh: 把数十个从 Flickr 抓取（2004–2020）的公开人脸数据集中的照片编号与元数据建立索引供用户检索；MegaPixels 运行于 2017–2020 年，2021 年以 Exposing.ai 重新上线。
exhibited: Ludwig Forum Aachen, Training the Archive 2020

works.title: VFRAME
works.description: A computer-vision toolkit for human-rights researchers that scans huge conflict-zone video archives for specific munitions, such as the 9N235 cluster submunition.
works.description_zh: 一套为人权研究者开发的计算机视觉工具，在海量冲突地区视频档案中搜寻特定弹药，例如 9N235 集束子弹药。
works.idea_en: Machine vision can be turned from the watcher's tool into a witness's tool, if someone builds the dataset for it.
works.idea_zh: 只要有人为它建好数据集，机器视觉就可以从监视者的工具变成见证者的工具。
works.method: Object detectors are trained on synthetic images of munitions made with photogrammetry, 3D rendering and 3D-printed replicas, then run over archives such as the Syrian Archive.
works.method_zh: 用摄影测量、三维渲染和三维打印复制品生成弹药的合成图像来训练目标检测器，再在 Syrian Archive 等档案上运行。

works.title: Data-masks
works.description: 3D-printed nylon masks evolved until face detection and recognition software accepts them as faces: portraits of a human as the machine imagines one.
works.description_zh: 一组三维打印的尼龙面具，经过“演化”直到人脸检测与识别软件把它们认作人脸：机器想象中的人的肖像。
works.idea_en: What a surveillance algorithm calls a face is a ghostly average that no person has.
works.idea_zh: 监控算法所说的“脸”，是一个没有人真正拥有的幽灵般的平均形状。
works.method: Face detection and recognition algorithms were reverse-engineered and genetic algorithms evolved forms that satisfy them, which were then 3D-printed (2013–2015).
works.method_zh: 对人脸检测与识别算法进行逆向工程，用遗传算法演化出能被它们接受的形状，再三维打印出来（2013–2015）。

works.title: URME Surveillance
works.description: The artist sells a photo-realistic 3D-printed prosthetic of his own face; anyone wearing it in front of face-recognition cameras is identified as Leo Selvaggio.
works.description_zh: 艺术家出售一副照片般逼真的三维打印“自己的脸”；任何人戴上它走过人脸识别摄像头，都会被识别为 Leo Selvaggio。
works.idea_en: If the system can only match faces, many bodies sharing one face make its records meaningless.
works.idea_zh: 如果系统只会匹配人脸，那么许多身体共用一张脸，就会让它的记录失去意义。
works.method: A resin prosthetic made from a 3D scan of the artist's face, launched via an Indiegogo campaign and shown with a face-tracking mirror installation.
works.method_zh: 根据艺术家面部三维扫描制作的树脂义面，通过 Indiegogo 众筹发布，并配有人脸追踪镜面装置展出。

works.title: Manifesto Collection
works.description: Knitted jumpers, trousers and dresses whose woven patterns make AI detectors label the wearer as an animal or object instead of a person.
works.description_zh: 一系列针织毛衣、长裤和连衣裙，织入的图案会让 AI 检测器把穿着者标注成动物或物体，而不是人。
works.idea_en: An adversarial example can be knitted: the machine's weakness becomes a garment you choose to wear.
works.idea_zh: 对抗样本可以被织出来：机器的弱点变成一件你可以选择穿上的衣服。
works.method: Adversarial patterns, likely optimised against YOLO-type real-time object detectors, are woven into knitwear with a computerised knitting machine; made in Italy.
works.method_zh: 针对实时目标检测器（很可能是 YOLO 一类）优化的对抗图案，用电脑针织机织入衣物；意大利生产。

works.title: Perception Engines
works.description: A series of abstract prints that ImageNet classifiers confidently recognise as a cello, a cabbage, a hammerhead shark or an iron, though people see only a few coloured strokes.
works.description_zh: 一组抽象版画：人只看到几笔色块，ImageNet 分类器却会自信地把它们认作大提琴、卷心菜、双髻鲨或熨斗。
works.idea_en: Art can be made for the machine's eye: the prints show which few marks are 'enough' for a classifier.
works.idea_zh: 艺术可以为机器之眼而作：这些版画显示，对分类器来说几笔就“够了”。
works.method: A constrained drawing system is optimised against an ensemble of ImageNet classifiers, and the results are printed as risographs and screen prints.
works.method_zh: 用一个受限的绘图系统针对一组 ImageNet 分类器进行优化，结果以孔版印刷和丝网印刷呈现。

works.title: Autonomous Trap 001
works.description: On Mount Parnassus the artist draws a salt circle with road markings around a self-driving car: a dashed line lets it in, a solid line forbids it to leave.
works.description_zh: 艺术家在帕纳索斯山上，用盐在一辆自动驾驶汽车周围画出道路标线：虚线让它开进来，实线却禁止它离开。
works.idea_en: A machine that obeys the symbols it sees can be trapped by those symbols, like a spirit in a magic circle.
works.idea_zh: 一台服从所见符号的机器，也能被这些符号困住，就像魔法阵中的精灵。
works.method: A salt circle with dashed and solid lane markings traps a car running the artist's own self-driving software; performed on 14 March 2017.
works.method_zh: 用盐画出带虚线和实线车道标记的圆圈，困住运行艺术家自制自动驾驶软件的汽车；2017 年 3 月 14 日完成表演。
exhibited: AI: Who's Looking After Me?, Science Gallery London 2023

works.title: Google Maps Hacks
works.description: The artist pulls a handcart of 99 second-hand smartphones through Berlin streets, and Google Maps turns the empty streets red with a virtual traffic jam.
works.description_zh: 艺术家拉着装有 99 部二手智能手机的手推车走过柏林街道，空荡荡的街道在 Google Maps 上变成红色的“虚拟拥堵”。
works.idea_en: A platform perceives the city through proxies; fool the proxy and the map, and then the traffic, follows.
works.idea_zh: 平台是通过代理信号来感知城市的；骗过代理，地图就会跟着变，随后交通也会跟着变。
works.method: Each phone runs Google Maps navigation, so the location data of 99 slow-moving devices is read as congested traffic.
works.method_zh: 每部手机都开着 Google Maps 导航，99 台缓慢移动的设备所发出的位置数据被系统读成交通拥堵。
exhibited: Japan Media Arts Festival 2021, Social Impact Award

works.title: How (not) to get hit by a self-driving car
works.description: A game installation in which players try to cross a virtual street without being detected by a self-driving car's pedestrian detector, disguising themselves to lower their detection score.
works.description_zh: 一件游戏装置：玩家要穿过一条虚拟街道而不被自动驾驶汽车的行人检测器发现，为此想办法伪装自己、压低检测分数。
works.idea_en: Every successful trick is an edge case the car would miss, showing whom its training data does not see.
works.idea_zh: 每一次成功的“骗过”都是汽车会漏看的边缘案例，暴露出训练数据看不见的是谁。
works.method: A camera feeds a pedestrian-detection model that scores each player live; winners can donate their edge-case data to improve the model or delete it.
works.method_zh: 摄像头把画面送入行人检测模型，实时为每位玩家打分；获胜者可选择把这些边缘案例数据捐出改进模型，或将其删除。

works.title: Deep Neural Networks are Easily Fooled
works.description: Anh Nguyen, Jason Yosinski and Jeff Clune evolved images, from static noise to abstract patterns, that state-of-the-art classifiers label with over 99% confidence as a king penguin, a starfish or a baseball.
works.description_zh: Anh Nguyen、Jason Yosinski 与 Jeff Clune 演化出一批图像，从雪花噪点到抽象图案，最先进的分类器却以超过 99% 的置信度把它们认作王企鹅、海星或棒球。
works.idea_en: A classifier's certainty is not seeing: it recognises features, not things.
works.idea_zh: 分类器的“确信”不等于看见：它识别的是特征，不是事物。
works.method: Evolutionary algorithms and gradient ascent generate images that maximise class scores of ImageNet- and MNIST-trained convolutional networks (CVPR 2015).
works.method_zh: 用进化算法和梯度上升生成图像，使在 ImageNet 与 MNIST 上训练的卷积网络对某一类别的得分最大化（CVPR 2015）。

paper.title: Deep neural networks are easily fooled: High confidence predictions for unrecognizable images

works.title: Accessorize to a Crime
works.description: Researchers at Carnegie Mellon printed colourful eyeglass frames that let a wearer dodge a face-recognition system or be recognised as someone else, such as a celebrity.
works.description_zh: 卡内基梅隆大学的研究者打印出彩色眼镜框，戴上后就能躲过人脸识别系统，或被识别成另一个人，比如某位名人。
works.idea_en: A face-recognition system can be steered by a few centimetres of pattern on the face.
works.idea_zh: 脸上几厘米的图案，就能左右一套人脸识别系统。
works.method: Adversarial perturbations are optimised only within an eyeglass-frame region, made smooth and printable, and tested physically against deep-network face recognition and Face++ (ACM CCS 2016; Sharif, Bhagavatula, Bauer, Reiter).
works.method_zh: 只在眼镜框区域内优化对抗扰动，使其平滑且可打印，并在现实中针对深度网络人脸识别和 Face++ 测试（ACM CCS 2016；Sharif、Bhagavatula、Bauer、Reiter）。

paper.title: Accessorize to a Crime: Real and Stealthy Attacks on State-of-the-Art Face Recognition

works.title: Adversarial Patch
works.description: Google Brain researchers made a printable, psychedelic sticker that, placed next to a banana, makes image classifiers see only a 'toaster'.
works.description_zh: Google Brain 的研究者制作了一张可打印的迷幻贴纸，把它放在香蕉旁边，图像分类器就只看到一台“烤面包机”。
works.idea_en: The machine's attention can be hijacked: one salient patch outweighs the whole scene.
works.idea_zh: 机器的注意力可以被劫持：一块醒目的补丁就能压倒整个场景。
works.method: A universal, scene-independent patch is optimised over many images, positions and scales against ImageNet classifiers such as Inception (Brown, Mané, Roy, Abadi, Gilmer).
works.method_zh: 针对 Inception 等 ImageNet 分类器，在大量图像、位置和尺度上优化出一个与场景无关的通用补丁（Brown、Mané、Roy、Abadi、Gilmer）。

works.title: Robust Physical-World Attacks on Deep Learning Visual Classification
works.description: A few black and white stickers on a real stop sign make a road-sign classifier read it as a 45 mph speed-limit sign from many distances and angles.
works.description_zh: 在真实的停车标志上贴几块黑白贴纸，就能让交通标志分类器在多种距离和角度下把它读成“限速 45 英里”标志。
works.idea_en: What looks like graffiti to a driver can rewrite the road for a self-driving car.
works.idea_zh: 在司机眼中像涂鸦的东西，却能为自动驾驶汽车改写道路。
works.method: The Robust Physical Perturbations (RP2) algorithm optimises sticker-like perturbations over varied physical conditions and tests them in lab and drive-by settings (Eykholt et al., CVPR 2018).
works.method_zh: “鲁棒物理扰动”（RP2）算法在多种物理条件下优化贴纸式扰动，并在实验室与车载行驶测试中验证（Eykholt 等，CVPR 2018）。

paper.title: Robust Physical-World Attacks on Deep Learning Visual Classification

works.title: Conflicted Phonemes
works.description: Wall-sized diagrams, made with designer Janna Ulrich, map the voices of twelve Somali asylum seekers whose claims the Dutch authorities rejected after a language-and-accent analysis. The maps trace lives of migration and camps that a single 'correct' accent cannot hold.
works.description_zh: 与设计师 Janna Ulrich 合作的巨幅图表，描绘了十二位索马里庇护申请者的声音；他们在荷兰经“语言与口音分析”后被拒。图中记录的迁徙与难民营经历，无法被一种“正确”口音所概括。
works.idea_en: When a state listens to accents to decide nationality, the voice is treated like a passport; mapping a voice's mixed history refuses that reduction.
works.idea_zh: 当国家通过口音来判定国籍，声音就被当成了护照；描绘一个声音混杂的来历，就是拒绝这种简化。
works.method: Research meeting in Utrecht (2012) with the rejected applicants, linguists and activists, turned into vinyl wall timelines and take-away A4 sheets; the maps were later submitted to a Dutch immigration judge and a UK asylum court.
works.method_zh: 2012 年在乌得勒支与被拒申请者、语言学家和社运人士开会研究，成果做成墙面时间线与可带走的 A4 单页；这些图后来被提交给荷兰移民法官和英国庇护法庭。
exhibited: Casco Office for Art, Design and Theory, Utrecht (commission, 2012)

works.title: The Freedom of Speech Itself
works.description: A 34-minute audio documentary on the UK's use of forensic speech analysis and 'voiceprints' to test the origin of asylum seekers' accents, heard among acoustic-foam sculptures shaped like the voiceprint of the word 'you'.
works.description_zh: 一部 34 分钟的音频纪录片，讲述英国如何用法证语音分析与“声纹”来检验庇护申请者口音的来源；观众在形似单词“you”声纹的吸音泡沫雕塑之间聆听。
works.idea_en: Voice analysis turns the way you speak into a territory; the state's ear, not your words, decides where you belong.
works.idea_zh: 语音分析把你的说话方式变成一块领土：决定你属于哪里的，不是你说了什么，而是国家的耳朵。
works.method: Interviews with lawyers, phoneticians, asylum seekers and Home Office officials edited with radiophonic techniques; foam sculptures are contour maps of the frequency and amplitude of two voices.
works.method_zh: 采访律师、语音学家、庇护申请者与英国内政部官员，用广播剧式的声音手法剪辑；泡沫雕塑是两个声音频率与振幅的等高线图。

works.title: The Whole Truth
works.description: An installation and audio documentary about voice-analysis lie detectors piloted by European, Russian and Israeli governments and used by border agencies and insurers. While visitors listen to interviews with the software's developers and sellers, a reverse-engineered lie detector judges those same voices in real time.
works.description_zh: 关于语音测谎仪的装置与音频纪录片：这类技术曾在欧洲、俄罗斯和以色列政府试点，并被边境机构与保险公司使用。观众收听软件开发者与销售者的访谈时，一台被逆向改造的测谎仪正实时判定这些声音的真假。
works.idea_en: Voice-stress analysis claims to hear beneath speech into the body; turning it on its own makers shows how arbitrary its verdicts are.
works.idea_zh: 语音压力分析号称能越过言语、听进身体；把它反过来用在制造者身上，便暴露了它判断的随意。
works.method: Reverse-engineered voice lie-detection software runs on the documentary's audio; three-channel video, stereo sound, a desk, chairs and artificial plants stage an interview room.
works.method_zh: 被逆向改造的语音测谎软件实时分析纪录片音频；三频道影像、立体声、桌椅与假植物布置成一间审讯室。
exhibited: Casco Office for Art, Design and Theory, Utrecht (commission, 2012)

works.title: Rubber Coated Steel
works.description: A 21-minute video staged as a tribunal for gunshots: it re-enacts the acoustic evidence from the 2014 killing of two Palestinian teenagers, where Abu Hamdan's spectral analysis showed that live rounds had been disguised to sound like rubber bullets.
works.description_zh: 一部 21 分钟的影像，被布置成审判枪声的法庭：它重现 2014 年两名巴勒斯坦少年遇害案中的声学证据；阿布·哈姆丹的频谱分析证明，实弹被伪装成了橡皮子弹的声音。
works.idea_en: Machine audio analysis can hear what human witnesses cannot, but the film asks whose silences a court is still unable to hear.
works.idea_zh: 机器音频分析能听见人类证人听不到的东西；影片追问的是，法庭仍然听不见谁的沉默。
works.method: Audio-ballistic analysis made with Forensic Architecture for Defence for Children International, visualising sound frequencies of recorded gunshots, re-staged as an empty courtroom with subtitles and silences.
works.method_zh: 与 Forensic Architecture 为保护儿童国际组织所做的音频弹道分析，将录音中枪声的频率可视化，再以一间只有字幕和沉默的空法庭重新呈现。

works.title: Machine Listening, a Curriculum
works.description: An open, evolving curriculum of reading lists, a library, prompts, interviews, commissioned texts, music and recorded online events on the politics and aesthetics of listening machines, launched with broadcasts for Liquid Architecture and Unsound in 2020.
works.description_zh: 一套开放、持续更新的课程：书单、资料库、练习、访谈、委托写作、音乐与线上活动录像，讨论聆听机器的政治与美学；2020 年随 Liquid Architecture 与 Unsound 的系列直播发布。
works.idea_en: Our devices now analyse and respond to sound, not just record it; machine listening is a field of knowledge-power that needs collective study and counter-strategies.
works.idea_zh: 设备如今不只录音，还分析并回应声音；机器聆听是一个知识权力领域，需要集体学习与对抗策略。
works.method: Open-source pedagogy platform (built on Pirate Care's curriculum tool) combining syllabi, archives and Zoom-era radio broadcasts.
works.method_zh: 开源教学平台（基于 Pirate Care 的课程工具），把教学大纲、档案与疫情期间的 Zoom 电台节目结合在一起。

works.title: After Words
works.description: An 8-channel sound installation of speculative scenes built from readymade audio in machine-learning datasets, from acted emotional speech to Google AudioSet, woven through a script written with and against a language model.
works.description_zh: 一件八声道声音装置，由机器学习数据集中的现成音频拼成一系列思辨场景：从演员表演的情绪语音到 Google AudioSet，并穿插一段与语言模型合写又与之对抗的剧本。
works.idea_en: Data is never mined, it is made: audio datasets are performances, often by actors, and every 'Hey Alexa' is a performance for the machine.
works.idea_zh: 数据从来不是“挖”出来的，而是“做”出来的：音频数据集是表演，常由演员完成；每一句“嘿，Alexa”也是一场为机器的表演。
works.method: Samples from the Toronto Emotional Speech Set, DCASE sound-event datasets and Google AudioSet, voiced additions by critical-data researchers, and an autoregressive language model's text, spatialised over eight channels (18 min loop).
works.method_zh: 采样自 Toronto 情绪语音数据集、DCASE 声音事件数据集与 Google AudioSet，加入批判数据研究者的配音与自回归语言模型生成的文本，在八个声道中空间化播放（18 分钟循环）。
exhibited: Data Relations, Australian Centre for Contemporary Art (ACCA), Melbourne (2022–23)

works.title: Blendie
works.description: A 1950s Osterizer blender that only responds to a person's voice: you have to growl, whirr and hum like a blender, and it spins at the speed and power of your imitation.
works.description_zh: 一台 1950 年代的 Osterizer 搅拌机，只听人的声音：你得像搅拌机一样低吼、嗡鸣，它才会按你模仿的音高与力度转动。
works.idea_en: Instead of the machine learning our language, we must learn its voice; control becomes mimicry and a strange empathy with an appliance.
works.idea_zh: 不是机器学我们的语言，而是我们要学它的声音；控制变成了模仿，也变成了与电器之间一种奇特的共情。
works.method: Custom hardware and software for real-time sound analysis map the pitch and loudness of the user's blender-like sounds onto the motor's speed.
works.method_zh: 定制的软硬件实时分析声音，把使用者模仿搅拌机时的音高与响度映射到电机转速上。

works.title: On the Apparently Meaningless Texture of Noise
works.description: A binaural sound essay on the 'dialect recognition software' used in German asylum procedures: it listens to the breaths, pauses and other paraverbal 'noise' that the software's training data tells it to ignore, and builds a counter-archive of voices and leaked training documents.
works.description_zh: 一篇双耳声音散文，关于德国庇护程序中使用的“方言识别软件”：它去聆听训练数据要求软件忽略的呼吸、停顿等副语言“噪声”，并用声音与流出的培训文件建立一份反档案。
works.idea_en: What a listening machine is trained to discard as noise is exactly where a migrant voice keeps its history.
works.idea_zh: 聆听机器被训练成要丢弃的“噪声”，恰恰是移民的声音保存其历史的地方。
works.method: Sound essay recorded at EMS Stockholm (2019), composed from annotated paraverbal features, voices and documents from German Federal Office for Migration and Refugees (BAMF) field offices; published online for the Akademie Schloss Solitude and ZKM web residencies.
works.method_zh: 2019 年在斯德哥尔摩 EMS 录制，由被标注的副语言特征、声音以及德国联邦移民与难民局（BAMF）各地办事处的内部文件构成；作为 Akademie Schloss Solitude 与 ZKM 网络驻留项目在线发布。
exhibited: HASH Award 2020, 2nd prize (ZKM / Akademie Schloss Solitude)

works.title: How Not to Be Seen: A Fucking Didactic Educational .MOV File
works.description: A deadpan instructional video in five lessons on how to disappear from a world of high-resolution cameras, satellites and aerial targets: hide in plain sight, become smaller than a pixel, live in a gated community, or be a woman over 50.
works.description_zh: 一部冷面幽默的教学影片，用五课教你如何在高分辨率相机、卫星和航拍目标的世界里消失：大隐于市、变得比一个像素还小、住进封闭社区，或者成为 50 岁以上的女人。
works.idea_en: Being seen is a matter of resolution; invisibility can be a tactic against machine vision, but it is also how the poor and disappeared are erased.
works.idea_zh: 被看见与否取决于分辨率；隐身可以是对抗机器视觉的策略，但也正是穷人与失踪者被抹去的方式。
works.method: Filmed partly at a disused aerial photo-calibration target in the California desert, mixing green-screen performances, 3D animation and parodies of training videos.
works.method_zh: 部分拍摄于加州沙漠中一处废弃的航拍校准靶标，混合绿幕表演、三维动画与对教学录像的戏仿。

works.title: Project Alias
works.description: A fungus-like 'parasite' that sits on top of a Google Home or Amazon Echo and keeps it deaf with a constant murmur; only when it hears the user's own chosen wake word does it go quiet and whisper the real one.
works.description_zh: 一个像真菌一样的“寄生体”，罩在 Google Home 或 Amazon Echo 上，用持续的低语让它“失聪”；只有听到用户自己设定的唤醒词时，它才停下噪声，替你轻声说出真正的唤醒词。
works.idea_en: You can negotiate with an always-listening machine by giving it a machine of your own that controls what it hears.
works.idea_zh: 面对“永远在听”的机器，你可以给它配一台属于自己的机器，由它来决定对方听到什么。
works.method: A Raspberry Pi with microphones and two small speakers runs a locally trained wake-word classifier; it feeds noise into the assistant's microphones until triggered.
works.method_zh: 树莓派连接麦克风和两个小扬声器，运行在本地训练的唤醒词分类器；被触发前一直向助手的麦克风输送噪声。
exhibited: S+T+ARTS Prize 2019, Grand Prize – Artistic Exploration

works.title: Objectifier
works.description: A camera-and-socket device you train by example: show it a gesture or situation a few times and it learns when to switch a lamp or radio on, turning the user from consumer into the trainer of a small AI.
works.description_zh: 一个带摄像头的插座装置，靠示范来训练：对它做几次手势或布置某个场景，它就学会何时打开台灯或收音机，让用户从消费者变成一个小型 AI 的训练者。
works.idea_en: Teaching a machine to see through examples makes its perception, and its misunderstandings, part of everyday domestic play.
works.idea_zh: 通过示例教机器“看”，让它的感知与误解都成为日常家居中的游戏。
works.method: A camera feeds a neural-network classifier on an embedded computer that controls a power socket; a companion app lets users record positive and negative examples.
works.method_zh: 摄像头把画面送入嵌入式计算机上的神经网络分类器，由它控制电源插座；配套应用让用户录入正例与反例。
exhibited: Copenhagen Institute of Interaction Design (CIID) final project, 2016

works.title: Paragraphica
works.description: A camera without a lens: it reads the place you stand in through data (address, weather, time, nearby places), writes it as a paragraph, and turns the paragraph into a 'photograph' with a text-to-image model.
works.description_zh: 一台没有镜头的相机：它通过数据（地址、天气、时间、附近地点）来“读取”你所在的地方，写成一段文字，再用文生图模型把这段文字变成一张“照片”。
works.idea_en: A camera can perceive without light; its picture shows how a machine imagines a place from data rather than what is there.
works.idea_zh: 相机可以不靠光来感知；它的照片显示的，是机器如何从数据想象一个地方，而不是那里真正有什么。
works.method: Raspberry Pi with a touchscreen queries open location and weather APIs, composes a text prompt and sends it to Stable Diffusion; three dials set data radius, noise seed and guidance scale, and the viewfinder form is modelled on the star-nosed mole.
works.method_zh: 带触摸屏的树莓派调用开放的位置与天气接口，组成文字提示后交给 Stable Diffusion；三个旋钮分别控制数据半径、噪声种子与引导强度，取景器造型参考了星鼻鼹。

works.title: AZ: Move and Get Shot
works.description: Six films assembled by a bot from motion-triggered surveillance cameras that Arizona landowners set up on the US–Mexico border to publish images of migrants. The cameras fired at any movement, so the archive fills with animals, wind and light as much as people.
works.description_zh: 一个机器人程序从亚利桑那州土地主架设在美墨边境的动作触发监控摄像头中收集图像，自动剪成六部影片。这些摄像头本为公开偷渡者的影像，却对任何动静都会拍摄，于是档案里满是动物、风和光，也有人。
works.idea_en: Delegating the watch to a motion sensor empties the surveillance of its intent: the machine sees everything that moves and understands none of it.
works.idea_zh: 把监视交给动作传感器，监视的意图就被掏空了：机器看见一切移动之物，却什么也不理解。
works.method: From 2011 to 2014 a bot checked the landowners' website every 24 hours, saved newly uploaded captures from six cameras to a local server and appended them algorithmically to six continuous films.
works.method_zh: 2011 至 2014 年间，一个机器人程序每 24 小时检查土地主的网站，把六台摄像头新上传的画面存到本地服务器，并按算法接进六部持续生长的影片。

works.title: Hidden Voice Commands
works.description: Security research showing that speech recognisers such as Google Now can be commanded by audio that sounds like noise to people, including black-box attacks on commercial assistants and a defence study.
works.description_zh: 安全研究：Google Now 等语音识别系统可以被对人耳而言只是噪声的音频所操控；论文包括针对商用助手的黑盒攻击与防御研究。
works.idea_en: The listening machine does not hear what we hear; the gap between human and machine hearing is a space where commands can hide.
works.idea_zh: 聆听机器听到的与我们听到的并不相同；人与机器听觉之间的落差，正是命令可以藏身的地方。
works.method: Iteratively distorts speech features (MFCCs) so that recognisers still decode a command while human listeners in user studies cannot understand it; tested against Google Now and an open-source recogniser.
works.method_zh: 反复扭曲语音特征（MFCC），使识别器仍能解码出指令，而用户研究中的人类听者却听不懂；针对 Google Now 与开源识别器进行测试。

works.title: Racial Disparities in Automated Speech Recognition
works.description: An audit of five commercial speech-recognition systems (Amazon, Apple, Google, IBM, Microsoft) on interviews with Black and white Americans, finding an average word error rate of 0.35 for Black speakers against 0.19 for white speakers.
works.description_zh: 对五家商用语音识别系统（Amazon、Apple、Google、IBM、Microsoft）的审计：用美国黑人与白人受访者的访谈录音测试，黑人说话者的平均词错误率为 0.35，白人为 0.19。
works.idea_en: Listening machines hear some voices worse than others; the gap comes from what their acoustic models were trained on, not from how people speak.
works.idea_zh: 聆听机器对一些人的声音“听”得更差；差距源于声学模型的训练数据，而非人们的说话方式。
works.method: Transcribed matched audio snippets from the CORAAL and VOC corpora with each vendor's ASR API and compared word error rates, isolating acoustic-model effects.
works.method_zh: 用各厂商的语音识别接口转写 CORAAL 与 VOC 语料库中匹配的音频片段，比较词错误率，并分离出声学模型的影响。

paper.title: Racial disparities in automated speech recognition

works.title: Conversnitch
works.description: A small device disguised as a light bulb that eavesdrops on conversations nearby; snippets are transcribed by anonymous Mechanical Turk workers and posted to Twitter.
works.description_zh: 一个伪装成灯泡的小装置，偷听周围的对话；录音片段交给 Mechanical Turk 上的匿名工人转写，然后发布到 Twitter。
works.idea_en: The 'listening machine' is partly people: automated eavesdropping runs on hidden human transcribers and ends in public broadcast.
works.idea_zh: 所谓“聆听机器”有一部分是人：自动化窃听依靠隐藏的人工转写员，最后变成公开广播。
works.method: A microphone and Raspberry Pi hidden in a lamp-socket housing stream audio to Amazon Mechanical Turk for transcription; the text is tweeted automatically.
works.method_zh: 藏在灯座外壳里的麦克风和树莓派把音频传到 Amazon Mechanical Turk 转写，文字再自动发到 Twitter。

works.title: Dark Matters
works.description: An interactive web experience and video installation about the absence of Black speech in the datasets used to train voice interfaces such as Alexa and Siri, told through 3D space, sound and storytelling.
works.description_zh: 一件交互网页作品与影像装置，关于 Alexa、Siri 等语音界面训练数据集中黑人语音的缺席，以三维空间、声音与叙事展开。
works.idea_en: A voice assistant can only hear the voices its datasets contain; the missing speech is a dark matter that shapes who is understood.
works.idea_zh: 语音助手只能听懂数据集里有的声音；缺席的语音像暗物质一样，决定了谁能被听懂。
works.method: Browser-based 3D environment built from speech-dataset analysis and recorded voices, shown publicly as a beta web piece and a 24/7 window-gallery video.
works.method_zh: 基于语音数据集分析与录音构建的浏览器三维环境，以公开测试版网页和 24 小时橱窗影像的形式展出。
exhibited: Squeaky Wheel Film & Media Art Center, Buffalo (2021)

works.title: The Dark Age of Connectionism
works.description: An Amazon Echo surrounded by microphones: every sound visitors make triggers Siri to ask the Echo a question about its politics and function, and to hear the answers visitors must learn to stay quiet around it.
works.description_zh: 一台 Amazon Echo 被麦克风包围：观众发出的每个声音都会触发 Siri 向 Echo 提出一个关于其政治与功能的问题；想听清回答，观众就得学会在它身边保持安静。
works.idea_en: An always-listening device reshapes behaviour: to escape its ear you must change how you exist in the room.
works.idea_zh: “永远在听”的设备会重塑人的行为：要躲开它的耳朵，你就得改变自己在房间里的存在方式。
works.method: Surrounding microphones detect nearby sound events and trigger scripted questions spoken by an Apple Siri voice to an Amazon Echo, which interrupts itself with each new sound.
works.method_zh: 周围的麦克风侦测附近的声音事件，触发用 Apple Siri 声音向 Amazon Echo 提出的预设问题；每个新声音都会打断上一个问题。
